No opaque trail pixel may lie outside its own compartment's floor tiles or its host face: head and source stamps may fill a full cell, body stamps are at most a 48 px lateral strip at m and l, and the Layout clearance read is designed (LY-8 d, FT-37). *Why:* "one trail per source" (FT-3) and the eye line trail -> source -> hatch (`ART:704`).
145	
146	**FT-14 Seam weep along the bead.** A SEAM subject's descriptor renders the medium's trail **along the raised Hull Grey weld bead** in the Y-sorted layer at the seam's host-face origin: mist along the bead for GAS, rim frost for HEAT, a bowed rim for SEAL_STRAIN on a seam hatch; its extent runs along the seam line per FT-8. The Graph **states the seam weep's descriptor** (`LSG:170`): `subject_kind` SEAM, `mode` `1 LEAK`, `medium` GAS, `acoustic` HISS, `sev` 1 while `A_seam` > 0, `intensity_pm` per LS-14 field provenance (never 0 while the weep physically flows, so never silenced by the closed-valve rule; the fixtures take `A_seam` 1 as `intensity_pm` 15, as given, and restate no expression) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, and counts its `since_steps` from the SeamRecord's `built_step`, a true onset, so the weep grows from the weld at the sev-1 rate with no GA-T dependency. The weep therefore draws at s-*trace* (sev 1) by the ordinary size table; there is no PROVISIONAL tag left on this row *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. **Legibility floor:** at `A_seam` 1 the density table gives `density_level` 1 and `cover16` 4 of 16, which on a 16 px puff lit only by the chest lamp can read as "nothing is wrong" on the first weld the player inspects; the seam mist therefore carries `COVER16_FLOOR` 8 (D.4), a minimum of 8 of 16 cells whenever the seam descriptor is drawn, and the still-image criterion AC-151 asserts that a reviewer identifies "mist along a seam" at `A_seam` 1, `k_auto`, lit. *Why:* the weld is hero shape #3 and "the ship's first failure point"; the carried element "a failure trail spreading along a weld seam while you watch" (`ART:166`); `LSG:228` must-prove (P5, P2).
147	
148	#### 3. Time, keys and reconcile
149	
150	**FT-15 Keys wake, polls move.** A notification handler stores the key set and returns; it never reads or draws (`PIPE:190`, PR-8 rule 3). In the next render callback the system (1) re-reads `failures()` and `compartment()` (and, for the provisional rows of FT-30, `node()` and `edge()`, whose continuous `flow` and machine `T` dirty no key) **once per Graph step** into the per-step poll cache (the Graph runs once per `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` 6 ticks = 0.1 s; `since_steps` dirties no key, `LSG:532`), (2) spawns, despawns and re-selects size and behaviour on `F/` and `N/`, band accents on `B/` and `C/`, and rebuilds anchors on `T` and `SEC/`, and (3) every frame reads extent, dullness and animation phase from the poll cache and `present_time`. The key-family reaction table is below. **Step detection, key union and overflow** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; these were unspecified)*: a Graph step is detected by comparing the read view's `step_no` (the counter `since_steps` is defined against, LS-14) with the `step_no` stored in the poll cache; the poll runs on a difference and on no other condition. Notifications arrive once per tick (P5) and the render callback may run less often than the kernel ticks (30 Hz rendering, a hitch), so the handler **unions** every key set received since the last callback (a set, no duplicates, order irrelevant: a spawn-then-despawn pair within the union is resolved by the poll, which is the truth); if the union grows past `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` 256, or an `ALL` is among the notifications, the callback treats the union as `ALL` (FT-16). *Why:* LS-20 (`LSG:201`) says keys wake discrete presentation only; PR-8 rule 3 and the kernel's CR-10.
151	
152	**FT-16 `ALL` reconciles in one frame.** On `ALL` (a restore, a derelict instantiation, or a cascade above `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` 256, `KERN:466`) the system performs **one full re-read reconciled against its node pool within the same render frame**, never spread over frames. Two logging thresholds apply, **neither a cut-off**, exactly as `STEP_BUDGET_MS` (4 ms) is for the kernel: `TRAIL_RESTORE_BUDGET_MS` [PLACEHOLDER, 8 ms] for a restore or instantiation (a full rebuild) and `TRAIL_RECONCILE_BUDGET_MS` [PLACEHOLDER, 4 ms] for an in-play `ALL`, which is a diff against the pool (D.7) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the single 2 ms threshold fired on every legal worst-case world)*. After a restore the trail set appears already grown, because extent is a function of `grow_steps` (a persisted-field difference, GA-T) and nothing "starts" on load. The consumer-side cost is D.7 `trail_reconcile_cost`, which cites the registry formula `dirty_key_budget` by name and never restates its expression. *Why:* the MVP worst case is about 38 keys and about 17 descriptors (`LSG:532`), so one-frame reconciliation is cheap and keeps "never suppressed" (FT-19) testable. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
153	
154	**FT-17 LIVE / STILL and dullness are two orthogonal axes.** **LIVE vs STILL** is `intensity_pm` > 0 vs = 0 (for the ten ids with no Graph `intensity_pm`, the per-row LIVE predicate of FT-30 and D.4 in its place; a row with no LIVE axis at all is DRAWN_STATIC, States and Transitions): STILL stops the drip and the moving-medium frames **and freezes the extent at the isolation step** (FT-8, GA-T); the static stamps stay and draw at the authored coverage of their size for the current `sev` (the system remembers no earlier density, FT-1, so "held" means "does not animate", not "recalled"). **Dullness** is a quantised, palette-locked ramp of the trail's mode age `mode_steps` (D.5 `dullness`, `DULL_STEPS` [PLACEHOLDER], `DRIED_AFTER_STEPS` [PLACEHOLDER]; *Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: it ramped on `since_steps`, so a pipe that wore for 30 minutes and then leaked was born at the dried stop*) applied to **static stamps only**: a frost fan goes from bright to a greyed fan, a scorch from rimmed to matte, a puddle to a stain. Moving media (drip, mist, debris) are never dulled, so a live leak keeps looking wet. There is **no third "DRIED" state**: a derelict's authored dead fault (`intensity_pm` 0, large back-dated `mode_steps`, `LSG:226`) and a home-ship leak isolated by a closed valve (`intensity_pm` 0, mode kept, `LSG:127`) obey the same STILL rule. With GA-T the extent freezes at the isolation step while dullness keeps counting `mode_steps`, so a leak isolated long ago looks old and one isolated a moment ago looks fresh, which is honest. **A live trail never shows the dried verdict through the Graph's own clocks:** the dried stop is reached only at `dull_pm` 1000 (D.5), that is `mode_steps` >= `DRIED_AFTER_STEPS` >= 7500, and `mode_steps` restarts at every mode entry and every sev change. One residual case remained: a leak isolated early, left, and reopened after `DRIED_AFTER_STEPS` steps is live with a dried-stop age. **Default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20) (Open Questions 6d): a LIVE descriptor is capped at `DULL_STEPS` - 2** (D.5 `dull_step_shown`), so no live trail wears the dried look at any age or through any clock; the cap releases on the frame the descriptor stops being LIVE, so the isolation lands the dried verdict in one palette step (intended: the leak is old and the valve is the player's own act; Edge Cases, AC-177) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. **The cap also reaches the ongoing rows with no flow axis** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review; the cap's own intent, no default of Open Questions 6d is changed)*: a `7 OVERLOAD` and a `27 PATCH_WEEP` descriptor exists only while the cable is over its rating or the patch holds, so its presence is its liveness. They have no LIVE/STILL axis, so before this amendment they sat in DRAWN_STILL, were never capped and showed the dried verdict after `DRIED_AFTER_STEPS` steps of an unbroken condition, the very look the cap forbids. They are now DRAWN_STATIC and are held at stop `DULL_STEPS` - 2 for as long as the descriptor exists, with no release (when the condition ends the descriptor ends: T5). **A `4 FREEZE` and a `9 SCRAM` are not capped, because each is a latched fault and not an ongoing condition:** a forced-FAILED FREEZE persists until thaw and a SCRAM until `reset_node`, so a frozen coolant run or a scrammed reactor on a derelict is a dead fault and its greyed sheath or matte scorch is its verdict (ET-4). Derelict Authoring's `pa_frozen` is authored as a forced-FREEZE dead fault that must read dried (DA-17, lint `DEAD_FAULT_NOT_DRIED`), and a cap on row 4 would make that lint meaningless; the re-review's wish that a live FREEZE never show the dried look is therefore declined for FREEZE (a pipe frozen for `DRIED_AFTER_STEPS` unbroken steps is a latched failure and its old look is honest) and kept for OVERLOAD and PATCH_WEEP. Rows 20 and 21 carry no age, so there is nothing to cap (D.5, AC-177). Fuel is the exception by medium: the pool follows `fuel_puddle_ml` (row 25), shrinking only as the Graph's puddle does, and the fuel stain's dullness is a **palette swap at the final stop only (`fuel_dried` is true only when `dull_step` is the last stop, D.5), with no intermediate stop and no dither** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: it flipped at half the ramp, so a live fuel leak could read dried at 6000 steps)*, because any mix of the fuel hue with a grey passes through the flesh band the sane world reserves for sanity (Visual/Audio). `DRIED_AFTER_STEPS` must be at least 7500 steps (12.5 min, the longest live MVP clock, `LSG:667` D.15) so no live trail reaches the dried look before its fault finishes. *Why:* three discrete states would need a presentation timer to tell STOPPED from DRIED (FT-1); the art bible chose one shader with state from the mask (`ART:1065`-`ART:1067`).
155	
156	| Axis state | `intensity_pm` | `mode_steps` (age of the current mode, GA-T) | Draws |
157	|---|---|---|---|
158	| LIVE, fresh | > 0 | small | stamp chain growing at `GROW_PX_PER_STEP[sev]` from the source, moving media at `density_level`, full-colour static stamps |
159	| LIVE, aged | > 0 | large | as above, static stamps dulled by D.5 (never to the dried stop before `DRIED_AFTER_STEPS`); the drip still wet (the moving medium is never dulled) |
160	| STILL, fresh | 0 | small | stamp chain only at the extent frozen at the isolation step, full colour; the valve was closed moments ago ("the drip stops, the frost stops growing": the extent is capped at `grow_steps` frozen at the isolation step, FT-8) |
161	| STILL, aged | 0 | large | stamp chain only at the frozen extent, dulled; an old isolated leak |
162	| STILL, dried (derelict) | 0 | authored very large (back-dated mode onset) | the verdict: greyed fan, matte scorch, ember-dim stain; **GAS rows have no STILL form** (FT-18) |
163	| No flow axis (DRAWN_STATIC: rows 4, 7, 9, 27) | n/a (reads 0 and means nothing) | any | the static stamp at the authored coverage for the current `sev`, dulled by D.5; rows 7 and 27 are an ongoing condition and are held at stop `DULL_STEPS` - 2, rows 4 and 9 are latched faults and are not *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |
164	
165	*(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the table previously promised "the frost stops growing" while D.2 kept growing without an isolation term.)*
166	
167	**FT-18 A gas leak at zero flow is empty by design.** `1 LEAK/GAS` (and `8 SEVERED/GAS`) at `intensity_pm` 0 draws **zero pixels**: "O2 failure leaves no trail (mist evaporates), read from absence" (`ART:697`), and no residue accent exists for GAS (a stain would suggest a false O2 history on a derelict). A sev-3 trickle therefore reads "wide, sparse plume". This GDD **reads the Graph's lint** (`LSG:1110`, which scans for a consumer that "suppresses a consequence-channel descriptor whose sev >= 1 from its physical channel") as: *no consequence-channel descriptor with `medium` != NONE and sev >= 1 may be hidden from its physical channel while it has flow; an empty STILL GAS plume is not suppression, because the physical flow is zero.* The reading is this GDD's, not the Graph's, and is listed in Open Questions as routed to the Graph owner (non-blocking). **`27 PATCH_WEEP` on a GAS subject (a patched duct or O2 tank) is the second drawn-and-empty case** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling G2; creative-director ruling on the specialist disagreement)*: it draws zero pixels, because the Graph states that a PATCH_WEEP carries no flow (LS-11) and a dry-seam residue is rejected (it would suggest a false O2 history on a derelict, the reason this rule exists, and it contradicts "read from absence"). The consequence-channel tell is the **HISS** that Adaptive Audio plays at the descriptor's anchor (FT-35), and it is not suppressed, so R17 (no consumer may suppress a consequence-channel descriptor's acoustic or physical channel) is met acoustically. Recorded as the explicit FT-18 note: the Graph owner is asked to confirm that reading (Open Questions 43); this system never draws a GAS weep mark. *Why:* the verdict grammar (P5); `ART:697`.
168	
169	**FT-19 Never cull an on-screen consequence-channel element.** Every descriptor with `medium` != NONE and sev >= 1 **whose trail's bounding box lies inside or crosses the camera field at the current ladder step k** has its stamps drawn that frame (subject to FT-18). The test is geometric and is made on the **polyline bounding box padded by one head cell** (the `STAMP_PX` of the trail's head size, 48, 96 or 144 px) intersected with the field, **not on the anchor point** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: an anchor-point test let a trail whose source sits off-screen but whose body crosses the view pop in as the source scrolled on, which is the suppression this rule forbids)*. Cost pressure is relieved first by reducers that change no pixel (FT-41), then by degrading moving media, in this order: frame count, then density, then `TRAIL_ANIM_FPS` halving, then far-from-beam frame hold; **never stamps**. Not drawing is permitted only for trails whose padded bounding box lies wholly outside the field (re-evaluated at every k, so a zoom-out reveals every trail), dormant sections (they emit no descriptors, `LSG:822`) and sev 0. Distance culling and darkness culling are forbidden: they are exactly the suppression the Graph's lint scans for (`LSG:1110`). *Why:* P1 via `LSG:144` R17 (no consumer may suppress a consequence-channel descriptor's physical channel).
170	
171	**FT-20 Pure variation.** Stamp variant, drip phase offset and fan flip come from `rng_derive(world_seed, "trail.vis", (subject_id << 20) | stamp_index)` (D.6), the pure hash the kernel defines (`KERN:470`, D.10); the kernel's H9 restricts *simulation* from wall-clock and global randomness, and a presentation caller of a pure hash violates nothing. `world_seed` is read as exposed through **the kernel's read view of `kernel.clock`** (`KERN:477`, `KERN:844`; CR-12 makes every `SIM` block readable by presentation; the confirmation that `kernel.clock` is registered class `SIM` is routed to the kernel owner, non-blocking). If that read is not available, the fallback `TRAIL_VIS_SEED_FALLBACK` 0 [PLACEHOLDER] is identical on every client and after every restore, only less varied. Engine global random functions and any random-number-generator instance are forbidden in this system (lint). *Why:* two crewmates must see the same frost fan (P1); a restore redraws the same trail (`LSG:829`).
172	
173	#### 4. Look: technique, bands, pixels
174	
175	**FT-21 Static stamps and stepped frames.** Static marks (frost fan, crust and sheath, scorch, glossy streak, puddle, hairline, crack and bent rib, bowed rim, rim frost, soot wash, and any dulled form) are **stamps** from the three-size sheets. Moving media (mist drift, drip, vent debris, wind streaks, AIRFLOW dust, arc pops, shimmer) are **pooled stepped sprite frames** at `TRAIL_ANIM_FPS` 12 [PLACEHOLDER] (the horror-rig precedent of 12 fps stepped, `PIPE:202`), with frame index from `present_time` (D.8), never from wall-clock or the tick counter (PR-8 rule 6). Particle systems are permitted **only** for venting at a BREACH or AIRFLOW opening, and only after a spike proves (a) per-instance positions floor to the base grid and (b) alpha is binary under nearest sampling (both unverified, HIGH risk); until then venting is stepped frames too. The "propagation frames" the art bible lists for the trail sheet are not needed and are dropped from the asset list: a growing front is a reveal threshold (FT-23), not extra drawings. *Why:* binary alpha and integer placement are exactly where particles are weakest; stepped frames satisfy both by construction (FT-22).
176	
177	**FT-22 Pixel integrity.** Nearest sampling; every item at an integer base-px position (placed by `floor`); **no per-node scale animation of any kind** (growth is stamp count, size swap and the reveal threshold of FT-23); `rotation` 0; hairlines, filaments and seams are **sprites, never runtime line draws** (PR-4 rule 10; the engine's 4.7 line-antialiasing change is moot for exactly this reason); alpha is binary (0 or 255) on every drawn sprite, including mist (a partially transparent mist is not pixel art); palette lock; minimum feature 2x2 px, except that a hairline is a **1 px Hull Grey run paired with a 1 px Void Steel shadow line (a 2 px composite, at least 4 px long)**, which the art-director ratified as a permitted 1 px element joining contour and glyph strokes (the *dried* 2 px coolant wet-run piece uses the same composite, V/A.3; *Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review*), an amendment candidate to the art bible's minimum-feature checklist (routed); no single-pixel noise; no violet and no flesh hue in any trail sheet or any dulled render; the alarm colour, the glowstick light colour and human (Tungsten) light appear in no trail. *Why:* `PIPE:110`-`PIPE:123`; `ART:1088`; `ART:422`-`ART:430`.
178	
179	**FT-23 Chain, reveal by threshold, density by dither.** A trail is an **anchor cap** at the source, **run** pieces chained along the polyline, a **tip** at the leading edge, **corner** pieces where Layout turns the line, and a **terminal** piece when the extent reaches its bound. The last run piece is revealed up to the extent by comparing its flow-phase ramp channel with an integer threshold (so a frost front is ragged and a scorch front radial with no extra art), never by scaling. Density (FT-5) is a **world-anchored dither of 2x2-px cells**, never partial alpha: the pattern keys on world base-px coordinates so it does not swim with the camera, overlapped stamps agree and every client draws the same pixels. Mechanism (runtime discard by coverage rank vs pre-authored dither sets) is an ADR candidate. *Why:* PR-4 rules 4 and 10; `ART:1065`-`ART:1067`.
180	
181	**FT-24 Never on a machine body, never on a crewmate.** OVERHEAT and SCRAM scorch, shimmer and glow are drawn at the **descriptor's anchor port or fitting** and on the floor and wall marks around the machine, never as an effect on the machine's body sprite (the corruptible module-body channel). Shimmer is a stepped frame sprite at the fitting; this system has no distortion shader of any kind. A trail is anchored to the fitting or edge, never to a machine's body, so a class (b) hallucination that redraws the body cannot move or hide the mark. *Why:* `LSG:168` (a lie can live only on the body channel); P4.

### Core Rules

*Every rule below describes what the player sees and when; node classes appear only in the Engine notes (the closing sub-heading of Visual/Audio Requirements) and the budget table (D.9), tagged as ADR candidates; the registry facts this system introduces are handed to the registry stage in `registry-candidates.yaml`, not duplicated here. Rule ids are `FT-n`; formulas are `D.n` in the Formulas section and are named, never restated, here; knobs are UPPER_SNAKE in Tuning Knobs. The system registers **no block, no step hook and no command**: the words "hook", "block" and "command" appear below only in sentences that say so. Registry constants are cited by their registered name and value (`TICK_RATE` 60, `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` 6, `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` 256, `W_MIN_WARNING_S` 10, `FLASH_MAX_PER_S` 3, `TILE_PX` 48, `V_WALK` 2 and `V_RUN` 3 px per tick); Graph-owned constants (`LEAK_HP`, `BREACH_HP`, `ALARM_SEV_MIN`, `A_HOLE_MAX`, `SEV_STEP`, `OPEN_END_RATE_PM`, `FREEZE_WARN_MC` and kin) are registered with source the Graph GDD (2026-10-27) and are cited by registered name and value; they are not this system's to change. A value this system needs from an undesigned neighbour or a Graph field the Graph has not defined is tagged **PROVISIONAL** with its owner; a value this system owns and no neighbour has fixed is tagged **[PLACEHOLDER: NAME]** with its registry candidate. Where the art-director or an advisor ruling changed a row of a table of record, the row was rewritten, not annotated.*

#### 1. Identity and channel

**FT-1 Statelessness.** Every visual property of every trail element is a pure function of `read_view` fields (`failures()`, `compartment()`, `node()` and `edge()`), Layout geometry and `present_time` (animation phase only). The system owns no timer, no fade, no grow counter, no smoothing accumulator, no "last seen" flag, no spawn-time stamp and no `Tween`; the only members that persist across a Graph step are pooled scene-node references, the per-step cache of the last `read_view` poll (which is a copy of truth and not state) and **the diagnostic latch set `diag_latch` (a set of `(log_id, subject_id)` pairs, FT-41), which no draw, reconcile or selection path may read** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the logging flags were previously outlawed by the statelessness lint they also needed)*. The test: the whole trail set can be rebuilt bit-identically from one `ALL` notification and `present_time`. Control-manifest lint line: "this system has no block, no hook, no command, no light node, no `true_value()` call, and no member that survives a Graph step except pooled node references, the last poll and `diag_latch`." *Why:* the Pipeline's PR-8 rejects exactly a presentation-owned fade countdown on a trail: the moment a trail's visibility depends on presentation state it is no longer the truth channel every hallucination is checked against (`PIPE:198`; P1, P4).

**FT-2 Truth channel.** Every node this system creates carries the TRUTH_PX grade of the Filter's PerceptionTag (registry: `perception_tag`). It reads `SIM` only, never `PERCEPTION_OUT`; it never calls `true_value()` (the Perception Filter is the only non-diagnostic caller); it has no "perceived" variant and no per-player trail. The Perception Filter may neither remove, alter nor add a trail, and this system's pixels are bit-identical with the Filter pass on or off. It works with either mask route the Filter chooses (a second viewport silhouette or per-element decomposition) and does nothing different when the mask is unavailable: in that case the Filter disables its own pass (`PIPE:735`). No sanity stage, setting, verb or hallucination class changes any trail property. *Why:* P4 "no lie is unfalsifiable"; the closed consequence-channel list (`LSG:168`); PR-10 (`PIPE:206`).

**FT-3 Descriptor-only drawing; one trail per source.** Every drawn element sits at a descriptor's anchor on a floor, wall face, seam, opening frame or fitting. No descriptor, no element. A source (one descriptor, keyed by the identity tuple `(subject_kind, subject_id, mode, medium, anchor)`) produces **one continuous trail, thickest at the source and never appearing at a node without upstream evidence on the connecting edge**. Two descriptors with different `mode` **or different `medium`** on one anchor draw as two trails in descriptor order (ascending `subject_id`, then `mode`, then `medium`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the tuple omitted `medium`, so a `26 SEAL_STRAIN` GAS and HEAT pair on one hatch would have merged into one trail)*. No orphan trail can occur: ambient decorative mist, steam or decals that are not Graph faults are not drawn by this system and Derelict Authoring may not place them. *Why:* "an orphan trail cannot occur" (`LSG:970`-`LSG:977`; `ART:669`; P1).

**FT-4 What this system never draws.** No meter, schematic, minimap, loop summary, numeric leak rate, health bar, damage number, hit flash, icon layer, beacon or alarm colour; nothing on a crewmate (Suit and HUD own body cues); nothing on a machine body sprite, gauge or inspect card (the module-body channel, FT-24); no web-grammar footprint (Horror Entities); no sound, and no gating on sound (Adaptive Audio leads, `IDX:41`); nothing that shows or hides Attention (P3). *Why:* `LSG:1003`; `ART:44`-`ART:55`; the anti-pillars.

#### 2. Signal-to-visual contract

**FT-5 Signal roles.** The three descriptor fields each drive one visual property, as the Graph documents them: `sev` selects the stamp size and the behaviour band; `intensity_pm` selects **density** (frame count, drip cadence, mist coverage as an ordered dither of 2x2-px cells, never partial alpha); the trail's **age** selects **extent** and **accumulation** (frost reach, scorch darkening, dullness): extent and accumulation read `grow_steps` and dullness reads `mode_steps`, the two per-mode age fields the Graph adopted as GA-T (LS-14; FT-8, FT-30); the Graph's `since_steps` counts from the first sev >= 1 descriptor or from `fail_since_step`, which is not the age of the current trail (the review finding behind GA-T), and is read only for the non-dominant seam weep, whose onset it counts truly (FT-8) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: GA-T is adopted in LS-14)*. A sev 3+ accent at the anchor (a wet collar, a heavy frost collar, a deep scorch pit) is drawn regardless of flow, so a pipe at hp 3999 with a trickle reads "badly damaged, barely flowing" and not "big leak" (exception: a gas leak at zero flow has no pixels at all, FT-18). Because `intensity_pm` is bucketed to 100 permille by the Graph, a density change always coincides with an `F/` key (D.4). *Why:* `LSG:158`-`LSG:159` document these roles; the fairness gate counts `sev` (`LSG:144`), so size tracks the Graph-guaranteed tell (P2).

**FT-6 Size ladder.** `trail_size` (D.1): **s (48 base px) at sev 1-2, m (96) at sev 3, l (144) at sev 4**; sev 0 draws nothing. Inside s there are two sub-tiers, *trace* (sev 1) and *full* (sev 2), so a sev 1 -> 2 step is still visible without a fourth size. For the integrity behaviour the sizes are the art bible's progression: s = **hairline**, m = **crack**, l = **bent rib or hole** (sev 4 = `A_hole` >= 32, `LSG:365`). Size is never produced by scaling a sprite (FT-22); it is a different drawing at the same pixel density. Size is a function of `sev` only (the single exception is the PUDDLE descriptor, which the Graph states at `sev` 1 but whose size follows its volume tier, D.2c), so a size change always coincides with an `F/` or `N/` key and needs no polling. **The sev-0 seam exception is retired** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: the Graph now states the seam weep as a `SEAM` descriptor, mode `1 LEAK`, `medium` GAS, `sev` 1 while `A_seam` > 0 (`LSG:170`), so a physically leaking weld seam draws at s-*trace* by the ordinary size table and no special case remains in D.1, D.2 or AC-11. The s/m/l semantics are **defined by this GDD** because the art bible names "the three sizes of 3.3 and 6.3" (`ART:1043`) and neither section defines them; the art-director ratified them with the trace/full amendment. Within one trail the chain tapers: stamp ordinal i from the source uses size index `max(1, size_idx - floor(i / TAPER_STAMPS))` (D.1; integer division), where `TAPER_STAMPS` **[PLACEHOLDER: `TAPER_STAMPS`]** (default 1) is the number of run stamps laid per size tier before the chain steps down one tier, so a larger knob tapers *slower*; the source is the thickest point. *Why:* m first appears at sev 3, which is `ALARM_SEV_MIN` 3 (`LSG:901`, Graph GDD), so the physical channel visibly escalates at or before the alarm ("alarm never first", LS-13 `LSG:144`, R17; P2); large stamps stay rare, which is the draw budget (`PIPE:616`).

**FT-7 Which size cells can be reached (finding, no new rule).** By the Graph's D.4 (`LSG:365`; worked example `LSG:381`, which gives hp 5000 -> sev 2 and a patched hp 6000 -> sev 1) a subject at `hp` just below `LEAK_HP` 4000 (`LSG:127`, Graph GDD) is sev 3 (`SEV_STEP` 1500); SEVERED is forced `sev = max(sev, 3)` (`LSG:367`, `LSG:240`). So a **live `1 LEAK` descriptor (GAS, COOLANT or FUEL), a `2 SHORT` and a forced `8 SEVERED` are always sev >= 3 at birth**: they draw at m or l and never at s. The s cells are reached only by pre-stage and ambient descriptors: `7 OVERLOAD` (sev 1-2), the `4 FREEZE` pre-stage (sev 1), the `5 BREACH` pre-stage hairline (sev 1-2, mode-5 STRUCT, confirmed by the Graph, `LSG:170`; pillar-critical for Pillar 2, see FT-32), `3 OVERHEAT`'s HOT shimmer (sev 2), `20 ATMO_COLD` (sev 2), `26 SEAL_STRAIN` (sev 1), the **seam weep** (`1 LEAK/GAS` on a SEAM, sev 1: the s-mist *trace* cell), `27 PATCH_WEEP` (sev 1 only: the s-*trace* cell of its medium's row, no new asset; *Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review*) and, by volume tier rather than by `sev`, a small `25 PUDDLE` (s-puddle, D.2c). **Consequence for the asset list:** author s-frost, s-scorch, s-hairline and s-strain **and s-mist (trace and full) and s-puddle** for the MVP (the earlier deferral waited on the Graph stating the seam-weep severity, which it now does). A live node `1 LEAK` (GAS, COOLANT or FUEL) is still always sev >= 3 at birth, so s-mist is reached only by the seam weep. *Why:* the pre-stage descriptors are the Graph's fairness tell (`LSG:127`); their trails are the s hairlines the player must learn to read. A wearing LEAK's own pre-stage is the WORN descriptor, which is module-body and draws nothing here (FT-32); a *patched* subject's pre-stage is `27 PATCH_WEEP`, which does. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review.)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*

**FT-8 Extent is a pure function, bounded twice.** The drawn length of a trail along its edge (D.2 `trail_extent`) is the **minimum of three things, never less than `MIN_EXTENT_PX`** (an m or l head stamp is revealed by D.10 like every other stamp, so at `grow_steps` 0 a sev 4 head shows 48 of its 144 px, threshold 42 of 127, and a sev 3 head 48 of 96, threshold 63; this is the intended "it begins" read and not an undrawn source): the physical edge length; the **age bound** `GROW_PX_PER_STEP[sev] x grow_steps` (clamped by `SINCE_CLAMP`), where **`grow_steps` is the trail's own age: the steps since the descriptor entered its current mode or last changed `sev`, frozen at the isolation step while a closed valve isolates it** (both are descriptor fields the Graph derives from three persisted onset fields, `mode_since_step`, `mode_key` and `isolated_at_step`, adopted as **GA-T** in LS-14, FT-30; they are not the Graph's `since_steps`, which counts from `fail_since_step` for a FAILED node or edge and from `warn_since_step` otherwise, so a LEAK that was a WORN node for half an hour would otherwise arrive fully grown, and every endogenous fault would arrive with at least the 100 fairness-gate steps already counted, which is 600 px at sev 3 and 1500 px at sev 4); and, for `4 FREEZE` only, the **temperature bound** `reach_px` (D.3 `frost_reach`; the whole edge for every other row; **for `1 LEAK/COOLANT` the temperature no longer limits the extent: it limits only how much of the run is drawn as frost, `frost_px`, D.2d**, user ruling D26) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. All arithmetic is integer; the result is floored to base px. A live descriptor therefore always draws the first `MIN_EXTENT_PX` 48 [PLACEHOLDER: `MIN_EXTENT_PX`] base px of its source stamp on its first step. **A severity change restarts the age** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; resolves the "sev rise redraws hundreds of pixels of history in one frame" finding by the onset request; restart-at-source is kept as a default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20), Open Questions 6c: neither the one-frame jump to the old age bound nor an `EXTENT_JUMP_MAX` cap is adopted)*: when `sev` changes, the Graph resets the mode onset (GA-T), so `grow_steps` is 0 on the new size's first frame, the new size's head stamp draws at `MIN_EXTENT_PX` and the extent regrows at the new severity's rate. The one-frame event is therefore a size swap and a restart at the source, never an old long mark inflated in one frame; a sev-4 bent rib that begins at the source and races along the rib at 150 px/s is the breach image (ET-3). The cost is that the longer extent of the previous, smaller mark is replaced by the short head of the new one; the descriptor is never undrawn (FT-19), and the head is the source, the thickest point. **Isolation freezes growth:** while a closed valve isolates a flow-fraction descriptor (`intensity_pm` 0 by the closed-valve rule, `LSG:127`) `grow_steps` stops at the isolation step, so a valve closed at `grow_steps` 50 on a sev 3 coolant leak (6 px per step) leaves the extent at 300 px for ever (a `4 FREEZE` sheath can still be pulled back by the temperature bound, D.3; a coolant leak's temperature pulls back only its frost part, D.2d) until the valve reopens (then `grow_steps` resumes from the live `mode_steps`, a one-time extent step bounded by the edge; Edge Cases). **The onsets are the Graph's, dominant-only and keyed (LS-14, adopted 2026-10-27 per the user ruling D30).** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* Phase 9 of the Graph keeps one onset pair per NODE, EDGE or SEAM, for the subject's **dominant** descriptor (the live descriptor of highest `sev`, ties to the lowest `mode` id), under the persisted key `mode_key` = `(mode << 3) | sev` (0 when no descriptor has `sev` >= 1): on each run, if the key computed from that run's state differs from the persisted `mode_key`, the Graph sets `mode_since_step` = `step_no`, `mode_key` = the new key and, when `isolated_at_step` > 0, `isolated_at_step` = `step_no`. **Consequence for seeding:** a seed that sets `mode_since_step` without the matching `mode_key` is overwritten on the first run and the trail is born at `grow_steps` 0 (a 48 px head, fresh colour), which would break the cryo-bay wake read and the ET-4 verdict; every fixture and every authored fault therefore seeds all three persisted fields (`FX-CRYO`: `mode_key` 11, FT-40; Onboarding and Derelict Authoring: FT-30, Open Questions 24 and 25; AC-171, AC-180). **Dormancy:** the Graph's M19 advances `mode_since_step` and a non-zero `isolated_at_step` of every subject in a section by the dormant interval on resume (LS-17), so `grow_steps` and `mode_steps` count only the steps the section ran; this system reads the result and adds nothing. **Non-dominant descriptors** (a seam weep beside a BREACH pre-stage; a FREEZE beside a LEAK): the Graph carries no onset for them and hands them the legacy `since_steps` as both fields (LS-14, Graph Open Question 39), which on a first frame can be hundreds of steps and would draw hundreds of px at once, the inflation this rule forbids. **Interim presentation, in force until the Graph publishes per-descriptor onsets for the RUN pairs that can occur (Open Questions 42); stateless, FT-1:** the resolver computes dominance per subject from the descriptor feed by the Graph's own rule, and a non-dominant descriptor draws as follows. A NODE or EDGE descriptor draws its **head stamp only** (extent `MIN_EXTENT_PX`, `dull_step` 0: a constant, so it neither grows nor inflates). The non-dominant **seam weep** (`1 LEAK/GAS` on a SEAM) reads `since_steps`, which the Graph counts from the SeamRecord's `built_step`, a true onset, so it keeps drawing at its true age and does not jump when a BREACH pre-stage of higher `sev` takes dominance. When a NODE or EDGE descriptor becomes dominant the Graph restamps its onset to that step (the key changes), so it regrows from the head it already shows: no frame shrinks and none inflates; a seam weep that returns to dominance restamps to its head, a rare, accepted shrink (Open Questions 42). A non-dominant descriptor is never undrawn (FT-19). The pair is tested on the hero seam: `FX-SEAM` with a mode-5 sev 1 and then sev 2 pre-stage added (AC-181). **Render-rate smoothing is off by default** (`TRAIL_EXTENT_SMOOTH` false [PLACEHOLDER]); when on, it interpolates only between the extent at `grow_steps - 1` and at `grow_steps`, evaluated from the committed tick and `tick_alpha`, never extrapolating (`KERN:298`); it needs no stored previous value (D.2) and it lags the committed value by up to one Graph step (0.1 s). Because the age fields dirty no key (`LSG:532`), extent is read from the per-step poll cache each frame (FT-15). *Why:* a pure function is restore-safe, MIRROR-safe, reduced-motion-safe and testable; a presentation grow timer is the rejected alternative of PR-8 (FT-1).

**FT-9 Growth invariants.** `GROW_PX_PER_STEP[sev]` is an **integer** (base px per Graph step; the pipeline places by `floor`). It must satisfy: (i) `GROW_PX_PER_STEP[1]` >= 1, so a sev-1 trail crosses a six-tile room (288 base px) in at most 288 steps = 28.8 s, inside the 30 s tell ceiling the Pipeline routed to this system (`PIPE:1081`, item 15); (ii) **`V_WALK` 2 px/tick (12 px per Graph step) < `GROW_PX_PER_STEP[4]` <= `V_RUN` 3 px/tick (18 px per Graph step)**, so a sev-4 single-edge trail is strictly faster than walking and no faster than running; (iii) monotone non-decreasing in `sev`. Placeholder table **[PLACEHOLDER: `GROW_PX_PER_STEP`]**: sev 1 = 2, sev 2 = 3, sev 3 = 6, sev 4 = 15 px per step (20 / 30 / 60 / 150 px/s); a 288 px crossing then takes 144, 96, 48 and 20 steps (14.4, 9.6, 4.8 and 2.0 s). Strict reading flagged for tuning: at the 100-step fairness floor (`W_MIN_WARNING_S` 10; the pre-stage descriptor's own `grow_steps` counts from its onset, so the 100 steps are the trail's steps, GA-T being adopted in LS-14) a pure sev-1 trail at 2 px per step has covered 200 px of 288, so invariant (i) holds but a "complete by 10 s" reading needs `GROW_PX_PER_STEP[1]` = 3 (300 px at 100 steps); the acceptance test will state which reading it checks (Open Questions). *Why:* "a failure trail propagating along a graph edge faster than you can walk" (`ART:224`); P2. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*

**FT-10 The cascade front owns the other half of the breach image.** The Graph lights successive edges one hop per run (`LSG:129`, LS-12; at most `MAX_SPREAD_PER_STEP` 32 new failures per run), each edge's trail starting at its own `grow_steps` 0. **No propagation animation state exists in this system**; the front's speed is the Graph's. The breach image is therefore true twice: single-edge sev-4 growth (FT-9 ii) and the cascade front. The art-bible carried element is satisfied by both. *Why:* `ART:224`; scope guard against absorbing the Graph. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*

**FT-11 The coolant frost fan and the coolant wet run are unconditional; the frost reach is not.** A `1 LEAK/COOLANT` descriptor always carries a static crystalline frost fan (a local stamp at the anchor and on the lagging) **at every temperature**, plus the drip; it draws **no drifting mist** (mist is O2's word). The fan's *spread as frost* along the edge and over the room's surfaces is bounded by the temperature (D.2d `frost_px`, FT-8): D.3 `frost_reach` maps the room's true `T` (polled from `compartment()`) to a maximum reach, with knots at the band edges [PLACEHOLDER: `FROST_REACH_PX`] (COMFORT and warmer: local stamp only; COOL/FROST edge: long; FROST/FREEZING edge: longer; FREEZING/DEEP_COLD edge: the whole edge) and **linear interpolation inside a band** [PLACEHOLDER: `FROST_REACH_INTERP` true; false restores a pure per-band step table], so frost stops growing when the band leaves FROST and retreats continuously as the heater warms the bay, with no stored state (the cryo-bay case, `LSG:839`); **what the retreating frost leaves behind is the wet run, not bare floor** (the paragraph below). **Knob constraint (fixture floor):** with interpolation the reach at the cryo-bay fixture band sits near the warm end of FROST, so `FROST_REACH_PX` must satisfy `frost_reach(T = -2000 mC)` >= 336 px (the far wall of `ART:142`, seven tiles); otherwise the far-wall frost of `ART:142` / `LSG:839` is unreachable whatever `mode_since_step` the fixture authors (*Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the fixture authors the mode onset, FT-8, FT-40*). The placeholder knots give 544 px at -2000 mC (D.3). **The coolant wet run (user ruling D26, Option A; Open Questions 6a).** At every temperature the chain that carries the frost fan continues as a **coolant wet run** out to the age-bound extent: the extent of D.2 has no temperature term for this row, `frost_px = min(extent, frost_reach(T))` of it is drawn as frost (the head fan stamp, always, then frost run stamps) and the rest, from the end of the last frost stamp to the extent, is drawn as wet-run pieces on a 48 px pitch whose width steps down with distance from the source (D.2d: 8, 6, 4, 2 px, each width over a quarter of the edge). The wet run is a static stamp, not a moving medium: a Void Steel body with a 2 px Coolant Ice edge line on one long side (no body at 2 px; the *dried* 2 px piece is drawn as the 1 px Hull Grey run plus 1 px Void Steel shadow line of FT-22, still 2 px wide, V/A.3) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, parallel-edged, with no spur, no fork, no blob, no glint speck, no iridescence and no angle. It is told from frost by having no crystalline branching; from a fuel puddle by hue (an Ice edge, not an Ember edge), by running as a strip of parallel edges and by having no blob or glint; from a hairline by a width of at least 2 px with an Ice edge and no fork; and from Horror's wet iridescent smear (`ART:565`) by being non-iridescent and edge-following from a coolant fitting with the frost fan at its source (FT-31). It sits on the band of the part of the polyline it follows (floor marks z +1, or the Y-sorted wall layer for a wall part), under the frost stamps; it dulls like every static stamp (D.5; its dried form is the "dried coolant run" of FT-12), and it freezes with the extent at the isolation step (FT-8). Frost and wet run never double a stamp: one chain, one piece per slot (D.2d, D.9 unchanged). *Why:* the followable gradient "thickest at the source" that FT-3 and Player Fantasy corollary 2 promise must hold at COMFORT, where the home ship spends most of its time, not only in FROST. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* **Room frost with no leak** (`20 ATMO_COLD`, row 20) is anchored at a **room-fixed tile** (the lowest `(row, col)` floor tile of `room_surface`, LY-23, that touches an exposed hull face, else the lowest `(row, col)` floor tile of the room; a function of Layout geometry alone, so a leak appearing or clearing at constant `T` moves no patch; the earlier "grows from the coldest leak" anchor relocated up to 24 patches when a leak toggled and had no tiebreak among several openings, and is withdrawn, Open Questions 6h) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, and its spread is the D.2b coverage ramp of the room's true `T` (0 at the COOL/FROST edge, full at the FROST/FREEZING edge; no age term and not the D.3 reach), *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(orchestrator ruling: the Graph's informative map reads "LEAK/COOLANT -> drip + mist, frost below 0 C" (`LSG:166`), and the Graph itself calls the map Failure & Trail's; shape redundancy outranks an informative table, because the colourblind backbone "O2 = drifting mist, coolant = static crystalline" (`ART:476`) must hold on the home-ship at COMFORT, where the game spends most of its time. Both clauses of the Graph's parenthetical, "+ mist" and "frost below 0 C", are therefore not rendered as written; a one-line informative rewording is routed to the Graph owner, non-blocking. Interpolation inside a band avoids a retreat jump of up to 480 px at a band key; the toggle exists so the literal per-band table can be restored.)* *Why:* P1 greyscale and colourblind redundancy (`ART:47`, `ART:314`, `ART:476`).

**FT-12 Hue from the loop, shape from the medium; the verdict grammar.** Each descriptor's colour is its **loop's hue** and its shape is its **medium's behaviour word**: mist (O2 loop), frost (coolant loop and cold surfaces), scorch (power), puddle (fuel), hairline -> crack -> bent rib (integrity). `medium` HEAT (OVERHEAT and SCRAM) has no behaviour row in the art bible and takes the hue of **the descriptor's `loop` field**, which the Graph now states (`LSG:170`): an OVERHEAT carries loop 3 (COOLANT) on a REACTOR or RESERVOIR and loop 2 (POWER) on a LOAD machine; a SCRAM carries 3 when tripped by OVERHEAT and 4 (FUEL) when tripped by fuel starve. The rim hue is therefore loop 2 Power Amber, loop 3 Coolant Ice, loop 4 Fuel Ember, chosen by a lookup on the field and by nothing else (so a reactor is rimmed Coolant Ice after an overheat trip and Fuel Ember after a starve trip, and an OVERHEAT on a fuel tank does not occur); no heat hue is invented *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the rule was written on the subject kind and disagreed with the Graph's loop provenance; the resolver now keys on `loop`, which makes the hue testable headless)*. **`4 FREEZE` of any medium draws the same frost sheath in Coolant Ice** (frost is the material of cold, as for `20 ATMO_COLD`); a frozen fuel tank (`medium` FUEL, `LSG:170`) is told from a frozen coolant pipe by the absence of a fan and a drip and by its subject (a tank fitting), and no coolant fan is ever drawn on it (Edge Cases); its thaw-burst, if any, is a new `1 LEAK/FUEL` descriptor drawn by that row. Compartment descriptors carry no loop: `20 ATMO_COLD` frost uses the coolant-ice hue because frost is the material of cold (shape, not loop, carries the meaning); `21 ATMO_HOT` soot and `24 AIRFLOW` dust are hue-less. Every behaviour carries **both contrast polarities** (a light element and a dark element) so it reads on lit and mid floor tones; scorch is a dark radial core with a loop-hue rim. The five behaviours stay distinct in greyscale and in a still frame: *mist drifts* (light, round clusters, no straight edge, no angle); *frost is static and crystalline* (lightest, hex-stair spurs branching at 60 degrees, no curve); *scorch is sharp and radial* (dark, straight spokes from one core, uneven lengths, an origin); *a puddle is glossy and flat* (dark, one convex blob, glint specks, no spokes); *a hairline runs along a rib or seam, never from a point* (mid plus dark pair, at most one fork per 16 px). Frost has one dendrite motif in three layouts: a **fan** (radial, at a coolant fitting or lagged elbow: `1 LEAK/COOLANT`), a **crust** (a linear run along an edge: `20 ATMO_COLD`, hatch rim frost, a dried coolant run) and a **sheath** (a continuous thick wrap over a pipe's lagging: `4 FREEZE`), so a fan at a fitting is coolant, a crust with no fitting is cold, and a sheath with no drip and no fan origin is a frozen pipe. **Scorch with a radial origin is a power arc; soot without an origin is heat** (`21 ATMO_HOT` draws a soot wash, not a scorch). Palette, reserved hues and exact values are in Visual/Audio. *Why:* `ART:314` (five behaviours), `ART:697` (verdict grammar), `ART:309` and `ART:399` (scorch dark, in its hue), checklist 13 (`ART:1216`, a trail out-contrasts every floor it crosses).

**FT-13 Wall mark plus floor run: one trail.** A descriptor on a wall-mounted fitting renders one continuous trail with a **wall part** (the Y-sorted wall layer, at the host face's sort origin) and a **floor part** (the floor-marks band) whose start point and direction Layout supplies (Layout `anchor_geometry`, LY-23, designed). Both parts share the single extent of FT-8, measured along the combined polyline, wall part first. Wall cells are 48, 96 and 144 px wide and at most 72 px tall (a wall front face is 72 px, `ART:1033`); floor cells are square. No opaque trail pixel may lie outside its own compartment's floor tiles or its host face: head and source stamps may fill a full cell, body stamps are at most a 48 px lateral strip at m and l, and the Layout clearance read is designed (LY-8 d, FT-37). *Why:* "one trail per source" (FT-3) and the eye line trail -> source -> hatch (`ART:704`).

**FT-14 Seam weep along the bead.** A SEAM subject's descriptor renders the medium's trail **along the raised Hull Grey weld bead** in the Y-sorted layer at the seam's host-face origin: mist along the bead for GAS, rim frost for HEAT, a bowed rim for SEAL_STRAIN on a seam hatch; its extent runs along the seam line per FT-8. The Graph **states the seam weep's descriptor** (`LSG:170`): `subject_kind` SEAM, `mode` `1 LEAK`, `medium` GAS, `acoustic` HISS, `sev` 1 while `A_seam` > 0, `intensity_pm` per LS-14 field provenance (never 0 while the weep physically flows, so never silenced by the closed-valve rule; the fixtures take `A_seam` 1 as `intensity_pm` 15, as given, and restate no expression) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, and counts its `since_steps` from the SeamRecord's `built_step`, a true onset, so the weep grows from the weld at the sev-1 rate with no GA-T dependency. The weep therefore draws at s-*trace* (sev 1) by the ordinary size table; there is no PROVISIONAL tag left on this row *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. **Legibility floor:** at `A_seam` 1 the density table gives `density_level` 1 and `cover16` 4 of 16, which on a 16 px puff lit only by the chest lamp can read as "nothing is wrong" on the first weld the player inspects; the seam mist therefore carries `COVER16_FLOOR` 8 (D.4), a minimum of 8 of 16 cells whenever the seam descriptor is drawn, and the still-image criterion AC-151 asserts that a reviewer identifies "mist along a seam" at `A_seam` 1, `k_auto`, lit. *Why:* the weld is hero shape #3 and "the ship's first failure point"; the carried element "a failure trail spreading along a weld seam while you watch" (`ART:166`); `LSG:228` must-prove (P5, P2).

#### 3. Time, keys and reconcile

**FT-15 Keys wake, polls move.** A notification handler stores the key set and returns; it never reads or draws (`PIPE:190`, PR-8 rule 3). In the next render callback the system (1) re-reads `failures()` and `compartment()` (and, for the provisional rows of FT-30, `node()` and `edge()`, whose continuous `flow` and machine `T` dirty no key) **once per Graph step** into the per-step poll cache (the Graph runs once per `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` 6 ticks = 0.1 s; `since_steps` dirties no key, `LSG:532`), (2) spawns, despawns and re-selects size and behaviour on `F/` and `N/`, band accents on `B/` and `C/`, and rebuilds anchors on `T` and `SEC/`, and (3) every frame reads extent, dullness and animation phase from the poll cache and `present_time`. The key-family reaction table is below. **Step detection, key union and overflow** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; these were unspecified)*: a Graph step is detected by comparing the read view's `step_no` (the counter `since_steps` is defined against, LS-14) with the `step_no` stored in the poll cache; the poll runs on a difference and on no other condition. Notifications arrive once per tick (P5) and the render callback may run less often than the kernel ticks (30 Hz rendering, a hitch), so the handler **unions** every key set received since the last callback (a set, no duplicates, order irrelevant: a spawn-then-despawn pair within the union is resolved by the poll, which is the truth); if the union grows past `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` 256, or an `ALL` is among the notifications, the callback treats the union as `ALL` (FT-16). *Why:* LS-20 (`LSG:201`) says keys wake discrete presentation only; PR-8 rule 3 and the kernel's CR-10.

**FT-16 `ALL` reconciles in one frame.** On `ALL` (a restore, a derelict instantiation, or a cascade above `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` 256, `KERN:466`) the system performs **one full re-read reconciled against its node pool within the same render frame**, never spread over frames. Two logging thresholds apply, **neither a cut-off**, exactly as `STEP_BUDGET_MS` (4 ms) is for the kernel: `TRAIL_RESTORE_BUDGET_MS` [PLACEHOLDER, 8 ms] for a restore or instantiation (a full rebuild) and `TRAIL_RECONCILE_BUDGET_MS` [PLACEHOLDER, 4 ms] for an in-play `ALL`, which is a diff against the pool (D.7) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the single 2 ms threshold fired on every legal worst-case world)*. After a restore the trail set appears already grown, because extent is a function of `grow_steps` (a persisted-field difference, GA-T) and nothing "starts" on load. The consumer-side cost is D.7 `trail_reconcile_cost`, which cites the registry formula `dirty_key_budget` by name and never restates its expression. *Why:* the MVP worst case is about 38 keys and about 17 descriptors (`LSG:532`), so one-frame reconciliation is cheap and keeps "never suppressed" (FT-19) testable. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*

**FT-17 LIVE / STILL and dullness are two orthogonal axes.** **LIVE vs STILL** is `intensity_pm` > 0 vs = 0 (for the ten ids with no Graph `intensity_pm`, the per-row LIVE predicate of FT-30 and D.4 in its place; a row with no LIVE axis at all is DRAWN_STATIC, States and Transitions): STILL stops the drip and the moving-medium frames **and freezes the extent at the isolation step** (FT-8, GA-T); the static stamps stay and draw at the authored coverage of their size for the current `sev` (the system remembers no earlier density, FT-1, so "held" means "does not animate", not "recalled"). **Dullness** is a quantised, palette-locked ramp of the trail's mode age `mode_steps` (D.5 `dullness`, `DULL_STEPS` [PLACEHOLDER], `DRIED_AFTER_STEPS` [PLACEHOLDER]; *Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: it ramped on `since_steps`, so a pipe that wore for 30 minutes and then leaked was born at the dried stop*) applied to **static stamps only**: a frost fan goes from bright to a greyed fan, a scorch from rimmed to matte, a puddle to a stain. Moving media (drip, mist, debris) are never dulled, so a live leak keeps looking wet. There is **no third "DRIED" state**: a derelict's authored dead fault (`intensity_pm` 0, large back-dated `mode_steps`, `LSG:226`) and a home-ship leak isolated by a closed valve (`intensity_pm` 0, mode kept, `LSG:127`) obey the same STILL rule. With GA-T the extent freezes at the isolation step while dullness keeps counting `mode_steps`, so a leak isolated long ago looks old and one isolated a moment ago looks fresh, which is honest. **A live trail never shows the dried verdict through the Graph's own clocks:** the dried stop is reached only at `dull_pm` 1000 (D.5), that is `mode_steps` >= `DRIED_AFTER_STEPS` >= 7500, and `mode_steps` restarts at every mode entry and every sev change. One residual case remained: a leak isolated early, left, and reopened after `DRIED_AFTER_STEPS` steps is live with a dried-stop age. **Default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20) (Open Questions 6d): a LIVE descriptor is capped at `DULL_STEPS` - 2** (D.5 `dull_step_shown`), so no live trail wears the dried look at any age or through any clock; the cap releases on the frame the descriptor stops being LIVE, so the isolation lands the dried verdict in one palette step (intended: the leak is old and the valve is the player's own act; Edge Cases, AC-177) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. **The cap also reaches the ongoing rows with no flow axis** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review; the cap's own intent, no default of Open Questions 6d is changed)*: a `7 OVERLOAD` and a `27 PATCH_WEEP` descriptor exists only while the cable is over its rating or the patch holds, so its presence is its liveness. They have no LIVE/STILL axis, so before this amendment they sat in DRAWN_STILL, were never capped and showed the dried verdict after `DRIED_AFTER_STEPS` steps of an unbroken condition, the very look the cap forbids. They are now DRAWN_STATIC and are held at stop `DULL_STEPS` - 2 for as long as the descriptor exists, with no release (when the condition ends the descriptor ends: T5). **A `4 FREEZE` and a `9 SCRAM` are not capped, because each is a latched fault and not an ongoing condition:** a forced-FAILED FREEZE persists until thaw and a SCRAM until `reset_node`, so a frozen coolant run or a scrammed reactor on a derelict is a dead fault and its greyed sheath or matte scorch is its verdict (ET-4). Derelict Authoring's `pa_frozen` is authored as a forced-FREEZE dead fault that must read dried (DA-17, lint `DEAD_FAULT_NOT_DRIED`), and a cap on row 4 would make that lint meaningless; the re-review's wish that a live FREEZE never show the dried look is therefore declined for FREEZE (a pipe frozen for `DRIED_AFTER_STEPS` unbroken steps is a latched failure and its old look is honest) and kept for OVERLOAD and PATCH_WEEP. Rows 20 and 21 carry no age, so there is nothing to cap (D.5, AC-177). Fuel is the exception by medium: the pool follows `fuel_puddle_ml` (row 25), shrinking only as the Graph's puddle does, and the fuel stain's dullness is a **palette swap at the final stop only (`fuel_dried` is true only when `dull_step` is the last stop, D.5), with no intermediate stop and no dither** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: it flipped at half the ramp, so a live fuel leak could read dried at 6000 steps)*, because any mix of the fuel hue with a grey passes through the flesh band the sane world reserves for sanity (Visual/Audio). `DRIED_AFTER_STEPS` must be at least 7500 steps (12.5 min, the longest live MVP clock, `LSG:667` D.15) so no live trail reaches the dried look before its fault finishes. *Why:* three discrete states would need a presentation timer to tell STOPPED from DRIED (FT-1); the art bible chose one shader with state from the mask (`ART:1065`-`ART:1067`).

*(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the table previously promised "the frost stops growing" while D.2 kept growing without an isolation term.)*

**FT-18 A gas leak at zero flow is empty by design.** `1 LEAK/GAS` (and `8 SEVERED/GAS`) at `intensity_pm` 0 draws **zero pixels**: "O2 failure leaves no trail (mist evaporates), read from absence" (`ART:697`), and no residue accent exists for GAS (a stain would suggest a false O2 history on a derelict). A sev-3 trickle therefore reads "wide, sparse plume". This GDD **reads the Graph's lint** (`LSG:1110`, which scans for a consumer that "suppresses a consequence-channel descriptor whose sev >= 1 from its physical channel") as: *no consequence-channel descriptor with `medium` != NONE and sev >= 1 may be hidden from its physical channel while it has flow; an empty STILL GAS plume is not suppression, because the physical flow is zero.* The reading is this GDD's, not the Graph's, and is listed in Open Questions as routed to the Graph owner (non-blocking). **`27 PATCH_WEEP` on a GAS subject (a patched duct or O2 tank) is the second drawn-and-empty case** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling G2; creative-director ruling on the specialist disagreement)*: it draws zero pixels, because the Graph states that a PATCH_WEEP carries no flow (LS-11) and a dry-seam residue is rejected (it would suggest a false O2 history on a derelict, the reason this rule exists, and it contradicts "read from absence"). The consequence-channel tell is the **HISS** that Adaptive Audio plays at the descriptor's anchor (FT-35), and it is not suppressed, so R17 (no consumer may suppress a consequence-channel descriptor's acoustic or physical channel) is met acoustically. Recorded as the explicit FT-18 note: the Graph owner is asked to confirm that reading (Open Questions 43); this system never draws a GAS weep mark. *Why:* the verdict grammar (P5); `ART:697`.

**FT-19 Never cull an on-screen consequence-channel element.** Every descriptor with `medium` != NONE and sev >= 1 **whose trail's bounding box lies inside or crosses the camera field at the current ladder step k** has its stamps drawn that frame (subject to FT-18). The test is geometric and is made on the **polyline bounding box padded by one head cell** (the `STAMP_PX` of the trail's head size, 48, 96 or 144 px) intersected with the field, **not on the anchor point** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: an anchor-point test let a trail whose source sits off-screen but whose body crosses the view pop in as the source scrolled on, which is the suppression this rule forbids)*. Cost pressure is relieved first by reducers that change no pixel (FT-41), then by degrading moving media, in this order: frame count, then density, then `TRAIL_ANIM_FPS` halving, then far-from-beam frame hold; **never stamps**. Not drawing is permitted only for trails whose padded bounding box lies wholly outside the field (re-evaluated at every k, so a zoom-out reveals every trail), dormant sections (they emit no descriptors, `LSG:822`) and sev 0. Distance culling and darkness culling are forbidden: they are exactly the suppression the Graph's lint scans for (`LSG:1110`). *Why:* P1 via `LSG:144` R17 (no consumer may suppress a consequence-channel descriptor's physical channel).

**FT-20 Pure variation.** Stamp variant, drip phase offset and fan flip come from `rng_derive(world_seed, "trail.vis", (subject_id << 20) | stamp_index)` (D.6), the pure hash the kernel defines (`KERN:470`, D.10); the kernel's H9 restricts *simulation* from wall-clock and global randomness, and a presentation caller of a pure hash violates nothing. `world_seed` is read as exposed through **the kernel's read view of `kernel.clock`** (`KERN:477`, `KERN:844`; CR-12 makes every `SIM` block readable by presentation; the confirmation that `kernel.clock` is registered class `SIM` is routed to the kernel owner, non-blocking). If that read is not available, the fallback `TRAIL_VIS_SEED_FALLBACK` 0 [PLACEHOLDER] is identical on every client and after every restore, only less varied. Engine global random functions and any random-number-generator instance are forbidden in this system (lint). *Why:* two crewmates must see the same frost fan (P1); a restore redraws the same trail (`LSG:829`).

#### 4. Look: technique, bands, pixels

**FT-21 Static stamps and stepped frames.** Static marks (frost fan, crust and sheath, scorch, glossy streak, puddle, hairline, crack and bent rib, bowed rim, rim frost, soot wash, and any dulled form) are **stamps** from the three-size sheets. Moving media (mist drift, drip, vent debris, wind streaks, AIRFLOW dust, arc pops, shimmer) are **pooled stepped sprite frames** at `TRAIL_ANIM_FPS` 12 [PLACEHOLDER] (the horror-rig precedent of 12 fps stepped, `PIPE:202`), with frame index from `present_time` (D.8), never from wall-clock or the tick counter (PR-8 rule 6). Particle systems are permitted **only** for venting at a BREACH or AIRFLOW opening, and only after a spike proves (a) per-instance positions floor to the base grid and (b) alpha is binary under nearest sampling (both unverified, HIGH risk); until then venting is stepped frames too. The "propagation frames" the art bible lists for the trail sheet are not needed and are dropped from the asset list: a growing front is a reveal threshold (FT-23), not extra drawings. *Why:* binary alpha and integer placement are exactly where particles are weakest; stepped frames satisfy both by construction (FT-22).

**FT-22 Pixel integrity.** Nearest sampling; every item at an integer base-px position (placed by `floor`); **no per-node scale animation of any kind** (growth is stamp count, size swap and the reveal threshold of FT-23); `rotation` 0; hairlines, filaments and seams are **sprites, never runtime line draws** (PR-4 rule 10; the engine's 4.7 line-antialiasing change is moot for exactly this reason); alpha is binary (0 or 255) on every drawn sprite, including mist (a partially transparent mist is not pixel art); palette lock; minimum feature 2x2 px, except that a hairline is a **1 px Hull Grey run paired with a 1 px Void Steel shadow line (a 2 px composite, at least 4 px long)**, which the art-director ratified as a permitted 1 px element joining contour and glyph strokes (the *dried* 2 px coolant wet-run piece uses the same composite, V/A.3; *Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review*), an amendment candidate to the art bible's minimum-feature checklist (routed); no single-pixel noise; no violet and no flesh hue in any trail sheet or any dulled render; the alarm colour, the glowstick light colour and human (Tungsten) light appear in no trail. *Why:* `PIPE:110`-`PIPE:123`; `ART:1088`; `ART:422`-`ART:430`.

**FT-23 Chain, reveal by threshold, density by dither.** A trail is an **anchor cap** at the source, **run** pieces chained along the polyline, a **tip** at the leading edge, **corner** pieces where Layout turns the line, and a **terminal** piece when the extent reaches its bound. The last run piece is revealed up to the extent by comparing its flow-phase ramp channel with an integer threshold (so a frost front is ragged and a scorch front radial with no extra art), never by scaling. Density (FT-5) is a **world-anchored dither of 2x2-px cells**, never partial alpha: the pattern keys on world base-px coordinates so it does not swim with the camera, overlapped stamps agree and every client draws the same pixels. Mechanism (runtime discard by coverage rank vs pre-authored dither sets) is an ADR candidate. *Why:* PR-4 rules 4 and 10; `ART:1065`-`ART:1067`.

**FT-24 Never on a machine body, never on a crewmate.** OVERHEAT and SCRAM scorch, shimmer and glow are drawn at the **descriptor's anchor port or fitting** and on the floor and wall marks around the machine, never as an effect on the machine's body sprite (the corruptible module-body channel). Shimmer is a stepped frame sprite at the fitting; this system has no distortion shader of any kind. A trail is anchored to the fitting or edge, never to a machine's body, so a class (b) hallucination that redraws the body cannot move or hide the mark. *Why:* `LSG:168` (a lie can live only on the body channel); P4.
