Should a radial look ever be wanted for a RUPTURE it carries a Void Steel hole centre and Hull Grey lips, and Horror's footprint stays hue-less and holeless.)* The Graph persists no footprint record (`LSG:196`, `LSG:912`); CHILL and BURN (at most `FOOTPRINT_MAX_Q` 20000 dJ, `LSG:196`, Graph GDD) rarely change a band and STRESS has no descriptor, so those three kinds have no trail (routed to the Graph owner as a VS-A candidate: a read-only footprint mark). Writes above `MAX_FOOTPRINTS_PER_STEP` (16) are dropped by the Graph, so a trail never shows a footprint the Graph did not accept (neither the registry's "per subject" nor the Graph's "in one run" scope wording is restated). **Known truth-channel hole (routed):** a GOUGE on a duct or cable surfaces only as the WORN descriptor (module-body, corruptible) or as a LEAK, contradicting "the hallucination hides the body, never the trail" for non-hull subjects; until the Graph owner closes it, **MVP Horror restricts GOUGE to hull segments; this restriction is binding on the Horror Entities GDD, not advisory** (creative-director ruling, CD-GDD-ALIGN stage 12). **Joint guarantee:** Pillar 4(a), "the hallucination hides the body, never the trail", is guaranteed jointly by this GDD (Graph descriptors, hull subjects) and by Horror Entities (web-grammar footprints: sound, frost, hull stress, light disturbance), so neither document may assume the other covers every footprint kind. Web-grammar marks (wet iridescent smear, branching rime, dust direction, filament twitch) are Horror's and share the floor-marks band; this system never draws coolant-fan-looking rime and tests for contrast collisions with Horror's marks. The coolant wet run (FT-11) is likewise never an iridescent or branching smear: it is non-iridescent, parallel-edged and edge-following from a coolant fitting with the frost fan at its source, and it is part of the collision fixture against Horror's wet smear (V/A.11 item 8, AC-79) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. *Why:* `ART:565`; P4(a).
221	
222	**FT-32 A patched subject weeps (`27 PATCH_WEEP`); the BREACH pre-stage is confirmed.** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: rewritten. The Graph adopted the patch weep, so the interim "a patch draws nothing" ruling, the switch-aware branch and the routed truth-channel hole are all withdrawn.)* A patch raises `hp` to at most `PATCH_CAP_BP` 6000, which is above `LEAK_HP` 4000, so the Graph clears the LEAK mode. A patched subject (`hp_cap` < `HP_FULL`, `hp` < `HP_OK`, no mode 1-9 live) then carries the descriptor-only id **`27 PATCH_WEEP`** instead of WORN (LS-11, LS-14; Graph OQ 23 closed by creative-director ruling "a patch weeps"): consequence channel, `sev` 1, `medium` by the subject's loop (GAS for a DUCT or O2 tank; COOLANT or FUEL for a PIPE, RESERVOIR or FUEL tank; ELECTRIC for a CABLE, junction or LOAD; STRUCT for the rest), `acoustic` HISS / DRIP / TICK accordingly, `intensity_pm` 0 and never silenced by it. A patched hull or seam already carries the mode-5 STRUCT pre-stage and emits no PATCH_WEEP. WORN (module-body, `medium` NONE) is not emitted for it, so the descriptor sits on the closed consequence-channel list and the Filter can neither hide nor fake it (P1, P4). **What is drawn (table of record row 27):** one small static s-*trace* mark at the fitting, per medium: COOLANT an s-frost spur (no drip), FUEL an s-trace puddle blob at the flange (ember edge, glint, no drip), ELECTRIC an s-scorch trace, STRUCT an s-hairline trace; **GAS draws nothing** (the HISS carries the tell: the FT-18 note). It is always static (no LIVE/STILL axis, DRAWN_STATIC), has no glow row, no extent and no accumulation (geometry class POINT_FIXED), and dulls by `mode_steps` under the ongoing-descriptor cap of FT-17. **The patch is a same-step handover:** the LEAK descriptor ends and the PATCH_WEEP appears on the same Graph step with `mode_steps` 0, so the fan, the wet run and the drip are gone the next frame (T5, a change the player caused) and the weep is there that frame, with no fade and no sparkle (anti-promise 4, AC-114, AC-70). **The three-way contrast** (a closed valve leaves the full mark, still; a patch leaves a small weep, static; a cap or a cut leaves nothing) is the reading grammar the Player Fantasy relies on. After `PATCH_DECAY_S` 240 the patch decays and the re-leak is preceded by the weep, a consequence-channel tell the Filter cannot corrupt, so the former truth-channel hole (the only pre-re-leak tell was on the module-body channel) is closed; the Onboarding line "patch it" (`LSG:839`) now ends the long carried fan but leaves the small weep, and should still be reconciled with the valve-based anchor moment (Onboarding's to do). **The hull case is resolved by the Graph** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: the BREACH pre-stage (hull or seam at `HP_OK` > `hp` >= `BREACH_HP`) is `mode` 5, `medium` STRUCT, `acoustic` TICK at flow zero, on the consequence channel and never WORN (`LSG:170`), so the sev 1-2 hairline of row 5 draws, the PROVISIONAL tag and the "blocking" label of the former Open Question 5 are retired, and the TICK is the k = 1 cue (FT-34). No Graph value is restated or changed here. *Why:* `LSG:127`, `LSG:222` are locked; a stale reading would give the consistency check a conflict. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the Graph's LS-11 and LS-23 carry PATCH_WEEP.)*
223	
224	**FT-33 MIRROR (VS-B).** The co-op summary carries each active descriptor as `(id, mode, sev, alarm_eligible, intensity bucket = intensity_pm / 100, since_steps, mode_steps, grow_steps)`, each age saturating at 2^24 - 1, 13 bytes each (`LSG:210`, LS-21), so a MIRROR client reads the same extent and dullness fields as the HOST and CR-10's identical presentation holds. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the summary now carries the two GA-T ages; the MIRROR legacy branch and its named extent mismatch are deleted, and Open Questions 10 is closed.)* The summary carries no `mode_key`, so a MIRROR client computes dominance from the `(mode, sev)` pairs of the summary by the same rule as FT-8. MVP is single-player; the path is exercised against a mocked summary through the descriptor-feed seam (AC-72) and is not an MVP gate. *Why:* the kernel's CR-10 requires identical presentation in HOST and MIRROR; P1.
225	
226	**FT-34 Zoom invariance and budgets at every ladder step.** Layout is in base px and identical at every integer zoom step k in [1, `k_auto` + 2] (`PIPE:161`, C6). Budgets (D.9 `trail_budget_at_k`) are stated **at every k and at 1080p, 1440p and 2160p, not at `k_auto` alone**: at k = 1 the camera field is up to 9x (1080p), 16x (1440p) or 36x (2160p) the area of the 640x360 default, so far more trails are on screen at once. The Pipeline's draw-call and particle-emitter caps are restated by name in Visual/Audio and Section D: floor marks `D_marks` 4-20 draws, at most 12 live particle emitters (mist at most 64 per trail, venting at most 128 per vent; "emitter" alone is Emitter State's record vocabulary, EM-3 and EM-4) re-expressed as frame-sprite counts for the stepped path, one Y-sorted layer of 50-300 draws, whole-frame 1000 draws (`PIPE:616`, `ART:1173`); if the sorted layer exceeds ~300 draws the remedy is per-row z-index bands for wall faces, never fewer props. Legibility gate: full legibility at `k_auto` and the first zoom-out; at k = 1 only polarity, hue blob and form class are guaranteed for m and l, and a sev 1-2 hairline (a 2 px composite) may not resolve, which is accepted and logged (not a licence to cull, FT-19, nor to add markers). **The non-visual cue that carries the flow-zero hull pre-stage at k = 1 (CD-GDD-ALIGN, stage 12):** the row 5 pre-stage has `intensity_pm` 0, so HISS and WIND (driven by flow) are silent; the cue is the **TICK** acoustic class, the hull groan the Graph's LS-22 Hull row names (`LSG:215`), played by Adaptive Audio at the descriptor's anchor on the consequence channel (FT-35); the Graph now assigns TICK to the flow-zero BREACH pre-stage (`LSG:170`), which closes the former FT-30 item (c) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. While the hairline is unresolved at k = 1 that TICK must exist for the descriptor; no marker, layer, icon or extra overlay is added, and the no-added-layer rule stands. *Why:* reflexion-log pattern 6 (an invariant asserted at the default must be re-checked when later decisions add reachable states).
227	
228	**FT-35 Audio independence.** This system plays no audio. The `acoustic` classes (HISS, DRIP, HUM_DROP, CLANK, WIND, TICK, SIZZLE, CREAK) are Adaptive Audio's, played at the same anchor from the same descriptor; a hiss with no visible mist (a dark room) is expected, not a bug; this system never waits for audio, and audio may lead visuals. Both systems take the anchor position from Layout (one source). Adaptive Audio is designed (`adaptive-audio-and-tells.md`): AA-24 plays the eight witness classes at the descriptor's anchor from its true fields, and AC-AA-117 discharges AC-144. *Why:* `IDX:41`.
229	
230	**FT-36 Accessibility toggles are read, not owned.** The system reads "reduced motion" and "reduce flashing" from the `SettingsStore` seam that the Chart Table & Menus layer owns (CT-18, CT-19; designed; the later Settings & Input Rebinding system, undesigned, replaces the page and keeps the seam) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* and applies FT-28 and FT-29 only; it owns no setting. **Defaults (user ruling D79, X10, 2026-10-27): "reduce flashing" is ON at first launch;** "reduced motion" keeps the pipeline default; the Chart Table & Settings owner sets both, this system only reads them. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* *Why:* `PIPE:847`.
231	
232	**FT-37 Containment (no orphan pixels).** No opaque trail pixel lies outside its own compartment's floor tiles or its host face. Run (body) stamps are authored so their lateral content never exceeds the corridor clearance (a lateral strip of at most 48 px at m and l); head and source stamps may fill a full cell. Clipping to a Layout floor mask and clamping the head stamp to clearance are rejected alternatives (the second would make `trail_size` depend on Layout, breaking FT-6). The Layout clearance read is designed (LY-8 d). **Corridor narrower than a head cell (closing-stage ruling, decided here):** because clipping and clamping are rejected, a corridor whose clearance is below the head cell of any size its anchor can reach (an anchor that can reach sev 4 needs 144 px of clearance at the head) is a **Layout content error** (a lint to Layout and Derelict Authoring, routed in Open Questions), never a runtime fallback; the acceptance fixture uses a corridor at least as wide as the head cell. **Interval reading (confirmed for Layout LY-8 d, 2026-10-27):** the 144 px is a free interval normal to the final run segment at each sample point of the floor run, not a square centred on the run line; the cryo-bay run 24 px from the north wall passes under it. *Why:* an orphan trail on the neighbouring room's floor would break FT-3 (`LSG:970`-`LSG:977`).
233	
234	**FT-38 MVP slice (what ships first, what waits).** **MVP:** every drawing row of the table of record for the ids the Graph's MVP slice emits (`LSG:228`: `1 LEAK` GAS/COOLANT/FUEL, `2 SHORT`, `3 OVERHEAT`, `4 FREEZE`, `5 BREACH`, `7 OVERLOAD`, `8 SEVERED`, `9 SCRAM`, `20`-`26` as emitted, `27 PATCH_WEEP` (every medium but GAS draws; GAS draws nothing, FT-18); `6`, `10`, `22`, `23` draw nothing) on the home-ship (5 compartments), derelict A (4) and derelict B (5); the stepped-frame path only (no particle node, FT-21); single-player (no MIRROR path, FT-33); the authored s cells s-frost, s-scorch, s-hairline, s-strain, **s-mist (trace and full) with `vfx_o2_mist_drift_s`, and s-puddle** (the seam weep is the ET-2 anchor moment and the Graph states its severity, FT-7, FT-14; *Amended 2026-10-27 — design review*); `27 PATCH_WEEP` reuses the s-trace cells of s-frost, s-puddle, s-scorch and s-hairline and adds no asset *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; one port shape (the round Foundry frame) for row 26 and the seam rows; variants s 2 / m 1 / l 1 (V/A.10 MVP cut); `TRAIL_EXTENT_SMOOTH` false; the six glow rows of V/A.6; the five drawing hazard groups of the eight MVP faults of `LSG:228`, each with a retained lit capture (AC-75). **Later:** particles for venting after spike S1; MIRROR parity (VS-B, FT-33; the summary already carries the two ages) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; the frozen-puddle presentation hint (VS-A, `LSG:838`); a read-only footprint mark for CHILL/BURN/STRESS (VS-A, FT-31); further port shapes and the full variant counts; the `DULL_STEPS` 8 scan matrix if the user chooses it (OQ 1). *Why:* the index names this system MVP for MVP item 2 (`game-concept.md`, MVP Definition); a slice that is only implied cannot be scoped into epics.
235	
236	**FT-39 The pure resolver *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; was only an "ADR candidate")*.** Every decision this system makes (state NOT_DRAWN / DRAWN_LIVE / DRAWN_STILL, `size_idx` and `sub_tier`, the chain, `trail_extent`, the reveal threshold, `density_level` and `cover16`, `dull_step`, `glow_step`, `fuel_dried`, hue token, band, patch tiles, puddle stamps, animation frame, the in-field test) is computed by one **pure `RefCounted` resolver**: `resolve(descriptor, ctx) -> TrailSpec` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the earlier argument list could not compute the in-field test, the LIVE predicates of SHORT and OVERHEAT, `n_arcs_room`, dominance or the smoothing)*, where `ctx` is one injected context object carrying: the node and edge views (`node(id)`, `edge(id)`), the compartment view, the geometry provider, the camera field and ladder step k, `tick_alpha`, `step_no`, `present_time`, settings, the knob table, the seed, and a **`hash_fn` seam** (default: the kernel's `rng_derive`; tests inject a stub, so the resolver itself references no random function, AC-164). A per-feed **pre-pass** `prepare_feed(descriptors, ctx)` runs once per poll and computes, from the feed alone, the per-subject dominance (FT-8), the arc counts over the world-fixed neighbourhood (D.8b) and the stable draw order; its result lives in the poll cache (a copy of truth, FT-1) and is passed in `ctx`. It reads no scene node, no autoload and no clock; every input is an argument (dependency injection over singletons: coding standards). The scene layer is a thin applier that writes a `TrailSpec` into pooled nodes and decides nothing. The resolver is the oracle for every `(auto)` criterion that follows and runs headless.

**FT-25 Draw bands.**

| Element | Band (Pipeline name) | z | Y-sorted | Sort origin |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Floor trails and puddles: frost run and crust, floor scorch, glossy streak, puddle, floor-plate cracks, soot edges | Floor marks | +1 | never | none: drawn flat, order among marks = authoring order; a mark never sorts above an actor standing on it and never below the hull it sits on |
| Wall trails and frame sprites: frost fan on the lagging or elbow, wall scorch, crack and rib along the wall face, hatch rim sprites, soot on lower faces | Wall layer (the one Y-sorted layer) | +10 | yes | the host face's sort origin, so the trail sorts with its face |
| Moving media: mist, drip, vent debris, wind streaks, shimmer, AIRFLOW dust | Dust and particles | +30 | no | "venting mist above a trail, below nothing" |
| Emissive layer (scorch, arc, ember) | shares its host stamp's band | as host | as host | as host |
| Not used | Floor (z 0), wall caps (z +20) | | | |

All bands stay inside every light range limit (`PIPE:132`-`PIPE:139`). Placement by `floor`; all marks sit under the hull-floor material, so an unlit trail never renders below the hull it sits on (`ART:1248`). *Why:* PR-5 band table; `PIPE:773` (hard dependency: layer assignment and nearest sampling that keeps a hairline a hairline).

**FT-26 Lit albedo marks.** Trails are lit marks under the hull-floor material (`max(albedo x ambient, floor tint)`); only scorch, arc and ember carry an emissive layer. In a dark room the trail is not seen, and that is correct: the hiss (Audio), the band cues (Suit) and the draught still tell. Acceptance captures are taken **lit**; the dark-room criterion asserts the descriptor and its acoustic class exist while no *non-emissive* trail pixel exceeds the hull-floor tint (a live emissive element may be visible and is the subject of FT-27). *Why:* "darkness is honest; light is a decision" (P1, P3); `ART:1248`.

**FT-27 No light and no emitter registration.** This system writes no light node and registers no emitter and no exposure. It supplies a **descriptor-to-glow data table** (palette hex, radius in base px, flicker class bounded by FT-29) in Visual/Audio; Emitter State registers the emitter from the same descriptor and Lighting renders it (designed; EM-17). The emissive layer on scorch, arc and ember stamps is an unshaded additive layer that **casts no light**. Whether a visible fault glow counts toward the web's exposure is not an art or presentation claim; it is decided by Emitter State's **EM-17**: "The emissive `_msk` trail glow on a sprite is an *unshaded overlay, not an emitter*, and exposes nothing", while the FAULT_GLOW *emitter* that `emitter.place` derives from the same descriptor "counts as exposure". This GDD supplies the ledger values Emitter State's D.11 multiplies (`GLOW_BASE_PM[key]` and `SEV_GLOW_PM[0..4]`, V/A.6; `EM:543`). *(CP-3, a light written here would illuminate a room without being an emitter the Attention system can see, so the narrower contract wins; EM-17 decides that the derived FAULT_GLOW emitter counts as exposure and the overlay does not.)* *Why:* P3 "emission is exposure".

**FT-28 Reduced motion.** Reduced motion holds every moving medium on its **authored hold frame** (frame 0 of each stepped strip; direction and density kept, so a mist that does not drift is still a mist), while extent, size, density and dullness continue because they are Graph state; `present_time` still advances. It never suppresses a trail, a hairline or audio. Each hold frame must read as its behaviour word in a still image (mist = peak-coverage frame with one wisp leaning along `dir`; drip = a hanging bead with a 2 px streak below it; vent debris = a mid-flight cluster; AIRFLOW dust = directional streaks with a tapered tail; arc = a steady glow at 60 percent of peak with the four static spark-tip pixels lit and no pops; shimmer = a static three-line wave). *Why:* `PIPE:232`, `PIPE:847`: reduced motion "never suppresses trails, tremor, hairlines or audio".

**FT-29 Reduce flashing and the arc number.** Arc and ember flicker is a **number**: `ARC_FLICKER_PER_S` (a derived, read-only value, D.8b, never a knob) <= `FLASH_MAX_PER_S` 3, counted per `flash_count` and `PIPE:228` (opposing >= 10 % luminance changes per rolling 1 s window). **One rate mechanism, one hold level** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; the earlier text divided the rate by the arc count and also put every arc on one shared world phase, two contradictory rules, and gave two hold levels, 60 and 88 percent)*: all live arcs flicker on **one shared world phase at one rate** `ARC_FLICKER_PER_S` (D.8b), so the counted transitions in any region equal one source's whatever the arc count; the rate is not divided by anything and cannot flip when the camera pans. The regional luminance clamp is met by **amplitude**, not by rate: each arc's emissive swing is scaled by the world-fixed arc count of its compartment (D.8b `swing_i_pm`), derived at the smallest ladder region (9,216 px at 384 x 216), so the clamp holds at every field and every pan. "Reduce flashing" replaces flicker by a held glow at the single level `ARC_HELD_GLOW_PM` (D.8b; 60 percent of peak), which is also the reduced-motion hold pose of an arc (FT-28, V/A.5). The light verbs are fixed so a decoy, a flare and an arc cannot be confused: **arcs pop**, deployables flicker, the cryo lamp gutters, pipes glow, fuel edges glint (a static highlight). **Counting unit (ratified 2026-10-27, user ruling D91 ii):** a flash is `ceil(n_transitions / 2)` opposing transitions in the rolling window, the registry `flash_count` expression (D.8b derives the rate from it). **Default (user ruling D79, X10):** "reduce flashing" is ON at first launch, so a first-run player sees the held glow at `ARC_HELD_GLOW_PM`, not arc pops; pops are the opt-out look and every pop capture states the setting (AC-64). **The held pose must still read as a fault, not as a fixture lamp or an OVERLOAD rim** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review; D79 is not re-opened, its consequence is answered)*: the user's default means the first thing most players ever see of a `2 SHORT` is the hold pose, so the hold frame carries **four static Power Amber spark-tip pixels** (2 x 2 px tips at the uneven spoke ends of the radial scorch, lit at the hold level) on top of the steady glow, which neither a Tungsten fixture lamp (no spokes, no origin) nor the `7 OVERLOAD` rim (a steady warm rim with no tips) has; the pop strip adds motion to the same tips, so the pop capture and the held capture differ only by motion. An art capture compares the three side by side (V/A.11 item 14, AC-63c). The sub-threshold and exemption weighting of D91 (iv) belongs to the HUD marks; the arc class keeps the strict regional ceiling of D.8b. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* *Why:* `PIPE:228` PR-13; `ART:979`; `ART` 3.2 and 2.2 reservations.

#### 5. Provisional rows, footprints, co-op, scale

**FT-30 Descriptor provenance (confirmed by the Graph, `LSG:170`); GA-T and the patched-subject pre-stage are adopted, three of the original five requests remain open and three narrow asks are added.** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the Graph's provenance paragraph now answers what this GDD asked on 2026-10-26, so the `PROVISIONAL` tags those questions carried are retired and this rule is reduced to what is still open.)* **Confirmed and in force:** `intensity_pm` is a flow fraction only for LEAK, the hole-area BREACH flow, AIRFLOW, SEVERED (`OPEN_END_RATE_PM` 500 permille of port cap, `LSG:772`), the seam weep and SEAL_STRAIN GAS (each per LS-14 field provenance). For `2 SHORT`, `7 OVERLOAD`, `3 OVERHEAT`, `9 SCRAM`, `4 FREEZE`, `20-23` and `27 PATCH_WEEP` the Graph defines none (it reads 0 and means nothing; Graph LS-14 field provenance lists the same ten), so those ten ids drive density from `sev` (`density_level` = `sev` in D.4), age from the trail age (FT-8), and the relevant true value from `node()` or `compartment()` (loading or flow for electric, `T` for heat and cold); LIVE for them is not `intensity_pm` > 0 but a **per-row LIVE predicate on a true value** read through `node()`, `edge()` or `compartment()` (D.4: `2 SHORT` live while the faulted conductor carries current, `3 OVERHEAT` live while the machine's `T` is above `OVERHEAT_OFF_MC`, cited by name; every other of the ten has no moving medium and is always drawn static, in the DRAWN_STATIC state), so a `2 SHORT` pops while current flows and goes still when the current reaches zero with the descriptor still present, whatever the Graph's `intensity_pm` reads; the static stamp always draws (FT-19) and only the moving media follow the predicate. The mode-5 STRUCT pre-stage and the SEAL_STRAIN HEAT/TICK branch are presented the same way and are never silenced by `intensity_pm` 0. Also confirmed: SEAM `since_steps` counts from the SeamRecord's `built_step`; COMPARTMENT and OPENING descriptors (20-26) carry `since_steps` 0 (so they use no age: D.2b); the seam weep is `1 LEAK/GAS`, sev 1, `intensity_pm` per LS-14 field provenance; `25 PUDDLE` is sev 1, `medium` FUEL, `intensity_pm` per LS-14 field provenance (the volume itself is read from `compartment().fuel_puddle_ml`, D.2c); `24 AIRFLOW` is sev 1 below `WELD_DP_WARN` and 2 at or above; an OVERHEAT carries loop 3 (COOLANT) on a REACTOR or RESERVOIR and 2 (POWER) on a LOAD machine, a SCRAM loop 3 (tripped by OVERHEAT) or 4 (FUEL, tripped by starve); a FREEZE on a fuel tank has `medium` FUEL; the BREACH pre-stage is `mode` 5, `medium` STRUCT, `acoustic` TICK at flow zero, consequence channel and never WORN; a patched subject at `hp` < `HP_OK` carries `27 PATCH_WEEP` (sev 1, `medium` by the subject's loop, `intensity_pm` 0 and never silenced by it) instead of WORN. This GDD never states a formula for the Graph's `intensity_pm` (AC-91): wherever this GDD names what `intensity_pm` measures it says "`intensity_pm` per LS-14 field provenance" and states no expression *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.

**Open requests, routed as one narrow amendment to the Graph owner (this GDD edits no Graph file):**

1. **GA-T, the time axis: ADOPTED by the Graph (LS-14, 2026-10-27; user ruling D30); closed.** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* The Graph's invariant check found no break (LS-14, "GA-T ... Result: no invariant breaks; GA-T is adopted"), so the contingency of the earlier text has lapsed and the legacy fallback is deleted. The Graph persists **three** onset fields per node, edge and seam, `mode_since_step`, `mode_key` and `isolated_at_step` (LS-21), and derives the two descriptor fields from them: `mode_steps = step_no - mode_since_step` (the age of the dominant descriptor's current mode and severity, restamped whenever `mode_key` = `(mode << 3) | sev` changes) and `grow_steps = max(0, (isolated_at_step if isolated_at_step > 0 else step_no) - mode_since_step)` (`mode_steps` frozen at the isolation step); COMPARTMENT and OPENING descriptors read 0 for both. The rule is **dominant-only**: one onset pair per subject, for its highest-`sev` descriptor (ties to the lowest `mode`), and the interim presentation of a non-dominant descriptor is FT-8's. `SHARED_SUMMARY` carries both ages (LS-21, FT-33). What is owed elsewhere: Derelict Authoring back-dates `mode_since_step`, sets `mode_key` to the fault's key and leaves `isolated_at_step` 0, wherever it back-dates `fail_since_step` (its DA-17 and the lint `DEAD_FAULT_NOT_DRIED` do neither yet: Open Questions 25, and ET-4 with AC-43, AC-44 and AC-171 are blocked at integration until they do: Gaps); the Onboarding fixture seeds all three fields, `mode_key` included (`FX-CRYO`, FT-40; Open Questions 24). The resolver also clamps `grow_steps` at `max(0, ...)`, so the formula is total whatever the Graph persists.
2. **Patched-subject pre-stage: ADOPTED by the Graph as `27 PATCH_WEEP` (LS-11, LS-14; Graph OQ 23 closed by creative-director ruling "a patch weeps"); closed.** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* Drawn by row 27, FT-32; the earlier interim ruling (a patch clears the trail the next frame and the subject is WORN) is withdrawn.
3. **Footprint kinds CHILL, BURN and STRESS** have no descriptor (FT-31, VS-A).
4. **Which mode a dead, unpowered electrical fault emits** on a derelict (a `2 SHORT` clears on repair or breaker open, `LSG:127`; a dead cable at `hp` < `HP_OK` with no mode live would emit WORN, which draws nothing), so the "matte scorch" leg of the verdict (ET-4) has a descriptor only if the Graph chooses to emit one.
5. **Whether a consequence-channel sev-1 companion exists for WORN** (a "sweat" on a wearing pipe), which would give the competence paragraph's early read a mechanism. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: a Pillar 2 / Pillar 4 decision owed with the Graph owner, Open Questions 45, no longer a non-blocking footnote; the Player Fantasy lists which failures have a floor pre-stage meanwhile.)*

**FT-39 The pure resolver *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; was only an "ADR candidate")*.** Every decision this system makes (state NOT_DRAWN / DRAWN_LIVE / DRAWN_STILL, `size_idx` and `sub_tier`, the chain, `trail_extent`, the reveal threshold, `density_level` and `cover16`, `dull_step`, `glow_step`, `fuel_dried`, hue token, band, patch tiles, puddle stamps, animation frame, the in-field test) is computed by one **pure `RefCounted` resolver**: `resolve(descriptor, ctx) -> TrailSpec` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the earlier argument list could not compute the in-field test, the LIVE predicates of SHORT and OVERHEAT, `n_arcs_room`, dominance or the smoothing)*, where `ctx` is one injected context object carrying: the node and edge views (`node(id)`, `edge(id)`), the compartment view, the geometry provider, the camera field and ladder step k, `tick_alpha`, `step_no`, `present_time`, settings, the knob table, the seed, and a **`hash_fn` seam** (default: the kernel's `rng_derive`; tests inject a stub, so the resolver itself references no random function, AC-164). A per-feed **pre-pass** `prepare_feed(descriptors, ctx)` runs once per poll and computes, from the feed alone, the per-subject dominance (FT-8), the arc counts over the world-fixed neighbourhood (D.8b) and the stable draw order; its result lives in the poll cache (a copy of truth, FT-1) and is passed in `ctx`. It reads no scene node, no autoload and no clock; every input is an argument (dependency injection over singletons: coding standards). The scene layer is a thin applier that writes a `TrailSpec` into pooled nodes and decides nothing. The resolver is the oracle for every `(auto)` criterion that follows and runs headless.

309	### States and Transitions
310	
311	*These are **derived render states**, recomputed from the poll cache and the camera field every frame and never stored (FT-1): a trail's state is a function of the descriptor and the camera, and nothing remembers what the previous state was. The system has no state machine of its own to persist, snapshot or restore; the table exists so the reaction to every Graph change is unambiguous and testable.*

338	### Interactions with Other Systems
339	
340	*Direction: "in" is data this system takes; "out" is data it gives. Status: **designed** = the neighbour's GDD exists with Status Designed and is cited by rule id and by line (lines as read on 2026-10-26; the rule id is the stable citation, because a sibling file still moves); **provisional** = no GDD exists and the contract is this GDD's proposal, to be repeated or rejected by the neighbour (reflexion-log pattern 4: only what this system must take or give is listed, never a neighbour's internals). **FT-40 Test seams and fixtures *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.** The resolver's inputs are the test seams: (1) the **descriptor feed** (an array of descriptor records with every `FailureDescriptor` field of LS-14, which already includes the GA-T fields `mode_steps` and `grow_steps`, and the feed's `step_no`; a Graph-integration fixture additionally seeds the persisted triple `mode_since_step`, `mode_key`, `isolated_at_step`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; (2) the **geometry provider** (`anchor_geometry`, `room_surface`, clearance: a stub returning a fixed polyline and tile set); (3) `present_time` (a float argument; no wall clock); (4) **settings** (`reduced_motion`, `reduce_flashing`); (5) the **knob table** (a data file, never constants in code); (6) the **seed** (`world_seed`); (7) the **logger sink**. Test tags: **(auto)** runs on the resolver or the poll logic headless, in the mandated CI command, under `tests/unit/failure_and_trail/`; **(auto-render)** needs rendered pixels (captures, bit-identity, dither, containment) and runs under `tests/integration/failure_and_trail/` on the named render job `ft-render` (a windowed or offscreen-capable Godot run on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK (R12; AC-83), never the headless job); **(lint)**, **(spike)** and **(manual)** as before. Fixtures are data files in `tests/fixtures/failure_and_trail/`: `fx_cryo.json`, `fx_tell.json`, `fx_row_oracle.json`, `fx_steady.json`, `fx_mvp_worst.json`, `fx_design_max.json`, `fx_seam.json`. **`FX-CRYO`** (the self-contained MVP cryo-bay fixture, owned by this GDD; Onboarding and the Graph's `LSG:839` fixture must match it): one compartment of 42 tiles at `T` -2000 mC (FROST), warming 8 mC per Graph step once the heater is on; one `1 LEAK/COOLANT` descriptor on a PIPE edge, `sev` 3, `intensity_pm` 600, `loop` 3, `acoustic` DRIP, anchor `anc_cryo_coolant` (geometry stub: wall part 0 px, floor part 336 px, a straight run along the north wall 24 px from it); `mode_steps` 56 and `grow_steps` 56 at the wake frame (`mode_since_step` = `step_no` - 56, **`mode_key` 11** = `(1 << 3) | 3`, the dominant descriptor's mode 1 LEAK at sev 3, `isolated_at_step` 0; seeded together, because the Graph's phase 9 overwrites a `mode_since_step` that has no matching `mode_key`, FT-8) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. **`FX-SEAM`**: one SEAM descriptor, `1 LEAK/GAS`, sev 1, `A_seam` 1 (`intensity_pm` 15), `since_steps` 0 at the weld, edge 288 px. **`FX-TELL`**: synthetic descriptors on a 288 px edge, `T` -12000 mC (below `FREEZE_WARN_MC` -10000 so the `4 FREEZE` pre-stage can exist, `LSG:127`; `frost_reach` = 480 + floor(12000 x 480 / 15000) = 864, at least 288), `4 FREEZE` sev 1, `5 BREACH` sev 2, `1 LEAK/COOLANT` sev 3, `5 BREACH` sev 4, each with `grow_steps` 0 at its first frame. **`fx_row_oracle.json`** is the **independent oracle**: one row per descriptor id and medium with its expected drawing/non-drawing, hue token and size reach, written from the table of record by hand and never generated from the resolver. The three budget fixtures (`fx_steady`, `fx_mvp_worst`, `fx_design_max`) are tabulated in D.9.

**FT-41 Cost, idle frames, warm-up, pool and one logging rule *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.** (1) **Idle frame:** a render frame with no new Graph `step_no`, no notification keys, no `anim_frame` index change and no camera-field change performs **zero scene writes and zero resolver calls**; it is the frame class `TRAIL_FRAME_MS_P99` budgets (D.7, D.9). (2) **Warm-up:** at load, before the first draw, one off-screen draw instantiates every material and shader variant the table of record uses, so the first leak of a session carries no compile hitch (spike S4, AC-84). (3) **Pool:** the node pool is pre-sized to `TRAIL_MAX_STAMPS` at load; growth past it is allowed, logged and never a cull. (4) **Pixel-neutral reducers come first:** write only the properties that changed, keep a retained per-trail draw list rebuilt on a key rather than per frame, and batch static stamps per room; each is verified bit-identical to the unreduced render (AC-163). Only then does FT-19's moving-media degradation order apply. (5) **One logging rule:** every diagnostic line (unknown descriptor id, missing geometry, each D.9 threshold, `ALL` over budget) is **edge-triggered**: a `(log_id, subject_id)` pair is latched in `diag_latch` on the rising edge of its condition, writes exactly one line, and re-arms when the condition clears (thresholds use `subject_id` 0; an unknown id or missing geometry latches per descriptor). No draw, reconcile or selection path reads `diag_latch` (FT-1).

#### 6. Descriptor-to-visual table of record

*This table is the system's table of record and the input to `/asset-spec system:failure-and-trail-system` (`LSG:979`); Visual/Audio refers to it and does not duplicate it. All eighteen descriptor ids have a row (ids 1-10, 20-26 and 27); mode 1 is three rows by medium; mode 8 inherits mode 1's row for its medium; id 27 is one row with a draw per medium. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* Behaviour words are the art bible's (`ART:314`). Band: **F** = floor marks (z +1), **W** = Y-sorted wall layer (z +10, host-face origin), **D** = dust and particles (z +30). "TRUTH" rows are consequence-channel and exact under the Filter; the four "draws nothing" rows say who renders that id's channel instead. `intensity_pm` and age columns say what each field drives (the age column is `grow_steps` for extent and accumulation and `mode_steps` for dullness, GA-T, FT-8); the PROVISIONAL tags on cells the Graph now states (`LSG:170`) are retired *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*, and a cell is still PROVISIONAL only where it depends on Layout geometry detail or on the open requests of FT-30. Sheets: `trail_shared` stamps (albedo and mask pages, plus normal and specular only on frost and puddle), stepped media strips `vfx_*`.*

#### 7. Key family -> reaction

| Key (`LSG:201`) | Meaning | Reaction in the next render callback |
|---|---|---|
| `F/<id>` | a descriptor's intensity bucket or appearance changed | spawn or despawn the trail; re-select size, density and LIVE / STILL |
| `N/<id>` | a node or edge's state, forced mode or severity transitioned | re-select size and behaviour; the sev 3+ accent on or off |
| `C/<cid>` | a compartment changed (one key per compartment per step) | re-read `T` (frost reach) and `fuel_puddle_ml`; update room frost and soot patches |
| `B/<cid>` | a band changed | band accents; the `ATMO_*` patch set |
| `L/<loop>/<anchor>` | a loop component summary changed | ignored (loop on/off is not this system's) |
| `S/<seam_id>` | a seam changed | re-resolve seam-bead trails |
| `T`, `SEC/<id>` | a structural change (a weld, a discard, a salvage) | rebuild anchors from Layout |
| `ALL` | collapse: restore, derelict instantiation, or more than `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` 256 keys | one full re-read within the same frame (FT-16) |
| (no key) | the age fields (`since_steps` and GA-T's `mode_steps` and `grow_steps`) never dirty a key (a `sev` change does: `N/`, and it resets the mode onset); neither do the continuous values behind the FT-30 LIVE predicates (`flow`, machine `T`) | read from the per-step poll cache every frame (FT-15) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |

### States and Transitions

*These are **derived render states**, recomputed from the poll cache and the camera field every frame and never stored (FT-1): a trail's state is a function of the descriptor and the camera, and nothing remembers what the previous state was. The system has no state machine of its own to persist, snapshot or restore; the table exists so the reaction to every Graph change is unambiguous and testable.*

| State | Entry condition (a pure predicate) | Exit condition | Behaviour | Who may cause entry or exit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| NOT_DRAWN | no descriptor for the subject; or `sev` 0; or `medium` NONE (WORN); or the id's row is a "draws nothing" row (STARVE 6, WORN 10, ATMO_THIN 22, ATMO_DECOMP 23); or the trail's bounding box padded by one head cell lies wholly outside the camera field at the current k (FT-19; *Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: it was the anchor point*); or the section is dormant (it emits no descriptors) | a descriptor appears with `medium` != NONE and sev >= 1 and the padded bounding box intersects the field | draws nothing | the **Graph** (descriptor appears or clears), the **camera** (field and ladder step k). Never Perception, sanity, a setting or a verb directly |
| DRAWN_LIVE | descriptor present, sev >= 1, `medium` != NONE, padded bounding box meets the field, `intensity_pm` > 0 (for the rows with a LIVE axis but no Graph `intensity_pm`, `2 SHORT` and `3 OVERHEAT`, the per-row LIVE predicate of FT-30) | `intensity_pm` falls to 0 (-> DRAWN_STILL), or the descriptor clears, or the padded bounding box leaves the field (-> NOT_DRAWN) | stamp chain at the extent of FT-8, moving media at `density_level`, static stamps dulled by D.5 | the Graph; the camera *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| DRAWN_STILL | as DRAWN_LIVE with `intensity_pm` = 0 (for `2 SHORT` and `3 OVERHEAT`, the LIVE predicate of FT-30 false) (a valve-isolated leak, a derelict dead fault; for `1 LEAK/GAS` and `8 SEVERED/GAS` the plume is empty by design, FT-18, and this is a drawn-and-empty state, not suppression) | `intensity_pm` rises above 0 (-> DRAWN_LIVE), or the descriptor clears or leaves the field (-> NOT_DRAWN) | stamp chain only, no moving media, dulled by D.5; static stamps at their authored coverage (nothing is recalled) | the Graph (a valve opening, a re-pressurised pipe); the camera *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| DRAWN_STATIC *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | descriptor present, sev >= 1, `medium` != NONE, padded bounding box meets the field, and the row has **no LIVE/STILL axis** (`has_flow_state` false): rows 4 FREEZE, 7 OVERLOAD, 9 SCRAM and 27 PATCH_WEEP (rows 20 and 21 are compartment patch sets with no age and use it too) | the descriptor clears or the padded bounding box leaves the field (-> NOT_DRAWN) | the static stamp at the authored coverage for the current `sev`, never a moving medium, dulled by D.5; rows 7 and 27 are an ongoing condition and are held at stop `DULL_STEPS` - 2, rows 4 and 9 (latched faults) are not (FT-17); a `27 PATCH_WEEP/GAS` is drawn and empty | the Graph; the camera |

Attributes inside DRAWN_*: size index (D.1) from `sev`; `density_level` (D.4); dull step (D.5); extent (D.2). **Dullness, glow decay (SCRAM) and extent are attributes, not states**: they change continuously with `grow_steps`, `mode_steps` and the room's true temperature and need no transition. Reduced motion and reduce flashing change an attribute (the hold frame, the held glow) and never a state.

| # | From -> To | Trigger | Condition | System action |

683	### D.9 `trail_budget_at_k`
684

686	
687	`D_FT = L_sets x P_trail x M_floor + sum over wall rows of M_wall(row) + I_wall + P_media`, with `M_wall(row)` = 1 + (1 if the row carries an emissive stamp, else 0), read from the table of record, and **`D_FT <= D_FT_MAX` conditional on spike S2** proving the per-instance data route (V/A.13) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the model had no 2D light-set term and no Y-sort interleave term; re-review: `M_wall` is data-driven, no longer charged as 2 per row unconditionally, and the conditionality is stated here)* ; `D_FT <= D_FT_MAX` ; `stamps_world = sum_desc(n_cover(E_desc) + 1) + n_patches_total + n_puddle_total` ; `stamps_world <= TRAIL_MAX_STAMPS` (logging threshold) ; `stamps_in_field(k) <= stamps_world` ; `layers_per_px <= TRAIL_OVERDRAW_MAX` ; mist mass per trail <= `MIST_MASS_PX_PER_TRAIL`, venting mass per vent <= `VENT_MASS_PX_PER_VENT` ; live particle emitters <= 12 only if the particle spike re-enables particles (otherwise 0)

689	The field at ladder step k is the Pipeline's (D.5 `zoom_ladder`, cited, not restated); the table below lists the values read from it at the three reference displays under `expand`. **The worst case is world-wide, not per field:** at the low steps the field is a multiple of the whole MVP world, so the binding cap is every active descriptor in the loaded world being on screen, and k only changes the on-screen pixel size and which cap is reachable. Because nothing on screen is culled (FT-19), the caps below are **logging thresholds and content-lint bounds, never runtime drops**. **Logging frequency (closing-stage ruling, decided here):** every threshold in this system is edge-triggered, one log line per crossing from below to above the threshold per session (re-armed when the value falls back below it), never per frame and never per step, matching the one-diagnostic-line-per-session precedent of the unknown-id and missing-geometry cases.

S2 reports three separate pass lines *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: (a) whether `CanvasItem` shaders receive per-instance data at all, (b) whether the four values survive exact 8-bit packing under `hdr_2d` (every one of the 256 levels of each channel reads back equal to the value written), and (c) 64 distinct parameter sets drawn in one batch without a draw split; S2 also decides whether the animation frame is shader-driven from a shared `present_time` uniform (D.7); the **fallback** if per-instance custom data is not available to `CanvasItem` shaders is to pack those four values into the instance `COLOR` channels and the `_msk` G ramp, at the cost of a coarser dull step; if neither route works, batching collapses toward one draw per stamp and `D_FT_MAX` is re-derived at the ADR. **The S2 result is recorded in `docs/engine-reference/godot/` (a new canvas-item file) and in an ADR before the first render story starts** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; **S3** stamp chaining at 48 / 96 / 144 and wall cells against 48 px tiles, the 24 px floor depth and the 72 px face, with a 2 px atlas gutter (no seam, no overhang into the cap band, no opaque pixel outside the compartment); **S4** material warm-up and Shader Baker (the first leak's frame time <= 1.5 x the render median); **S5** the arc flash scan with glow on (two l arcs in one region, and two l arcs in adjacent compartments: `F` <= 3 in every 1 s window per light, region and frame mean) and the timing of an `ALL` reconcile at `fx_mvp_worst` (661 stamps) and `fx_design_max` (618), pass thresholds in D.7; **S6** the truth-channel mask under both Filter routes (Filter-owned); **S7** lit Coolant Ice against the glow threshold at beam centre (no bloom on any lit trail sprite at any light energy Lighting allows: Coolant Ice's blue channel passes 1.0 at a beam-centre energy of about 1.10 under `hdr_2d`, so the glow threshold must sit above the brightest lit trail albedo and below the emissive layers' peak; Lighting decides the mechanism).

| TR-ftrail-027 | Non-dominant descriptors per subject (dominance by highest sev, ties to lowest mode) draw head stamp only at `MIN_EXTENT_PX` (except the seam weep, which uses `since_steps`); dominance is computed statelessly in the feed pre-pass and a MIRROR client derives it from summary `(mode, sev)` pairs. | Core | FT-8, FT-33, FT-39 |

- `resolve(descriptor, ctx) -> TrailSpec` and `prepare_feed(descriptors, ctx)` (pure RefCounted resolver, FT-39).
- `TrailSpec` fields: state (NOT_DRAWN / DRAWN_LIVE / DRAWN_STILL / DRAWN_STATIC), size_idx, sub_tier, chain, trail_extent, reveal threshold, density_level, cover16, dull_step, glow_step, fuel_dried, hue token, band, anim frame.
- Table of record: descriptor-to-visual rows for ids 1-10, 20-27 (FT table section 6).
- Descriptor-to-glow data table: `GLOW_BASE_PM[key]`, `SEV_GLOW_PM[0..4]` plus palette hex, radius_px, flicker class (V/A.6; read by Emitter State).

- Internal member `diag_latch` (set of `(log_id, subject_id)`).
- Knob table (data file): `MIN_EXTENT_PX`, `GROW_PX_PER_STEP`, `TAPER_STAMPS`, `FROST_REACH_PX`, `FROST_REACH_INTERP`, `DULL_STEPS`, `DRIED_AFTER_STEPS`, `ACC_STEPS`, `ACC_STEP_LEN`, `COVER16_FLOOR`, `TRAIL_ANIM_FPS`, `TRAIL_EXTENT_SMOOTH`, `TRAIL_MAX_STAMPS`, `TRAIL_RESTORE_BUDGET_MS`, `TRAIL_RECONCILE_BUDGET_MS`, `D_FT_MAX`, `L_SETS`, `I_WALL`, `TRAIL_VIS_SEED_FALLBACK`, `PATCH_MAX_PER_ROOM`, `PUDDLE_MAX_STAMPS`.
- Asset stems: `trail_cool_frost_*`, `trail_cool_wet_*`, `trail_fuel_puddle_*`, `trail_pwr_scorch_*`, `trail_hull_*`, `vfx_o2_mist_drift_*`, `vfx_*` strips, `trail_shared` atlas.
- Fixtures: FX-CRYO, FX-SEAM, FX-TELL.

## Consumes

- Life-Support Graph: `read_view` -> `failures(filter)` (FailureDescriptor per LS-14 incl. `mode_steps`, `grow_steps`, id 27), `compartment(cid)` (T, band_t, fuel_puddle_ml), `node(id)`, `edge(id)`; dirty keys `F/`, `N/`, `B/`, `C/`, `S/`, `T`, `SEC/`, `L/`, `ALL`; constants `W_MIN_WARNING_S`, `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS`, `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS`, `HATCH_DT_FROST_MC`, `WELD_DP_WARN`, `OPEN_END_RATE_PM`; persisted onset triple (LS-14/LS-21); `SHARED_SUMMARY` (LS-21).
- Pixel-Perfect Render Pipeline & Camera: `present_time` (PR-9), `tick_alpha`, ladder step k and camera field, band table, PR-4 pixel rules, PR-8 presentation contract, PR-10 truth-channel mask, PR-13 flash clamp, PR-14 reduced motion.
- Command & Simulation Kernel: PRESENTATION subscriber class, notifications `(block_id, tick, change_keys)`, `rng_derive(world_seed, stream, counter)`, `kernel.clock` read view (world_seed), CR-10/11/12.
- Ship Section & Layout: `anchor_geometry(anchor)`, `room_surface(compartment_id)`, corridor clearance (LY-8, LY-23), section body-frame offset.
- Chart Table & Menus: `SettingsStore` seam (reduced motion, reduce flashing; CT-18, CT-19).
- Perception Filter: TRUTH_PX `PerceptionTag` and mask-route contract (PR-10).
- Emitter State (consumer of glow table, EM-17), Adaptive Audio (shares anchors/acoustic classes, plays all sound), Horror Entities (shared floor-marks band, GOUGE hull-only), Derelict Authoring and Onboarding (must seed all three onset fields), Lighting (glow threshold above lit trail albedo), Save/Load (SL-17, no block).

## Engine risk

- CanvasItem shader per-instance data route (instance uniforms / MultiMesh custom data / COLOR packing) and exact 8-bit packing under `hdr_2d` (spike S2, `[UNV]`): HIGH.
- `hdr_2d` / glow threshold vs lit trail albedo (spike S7; bloom must not hit lit sprites): HIGH.
- Shader Baker pre-compilation / material warm-up (4.5, spike S4): HIGH.
- GPUParticles2D `process_time`/`process_time_residual` rename and `restart(keep_seed)` (4.7; only if venting leaves stepped frames, spike S1): HIGH.
- Canvas line-drawing antialiasing change in 4.7 (moot, lines are sprites): MEDIUM (noted, avoided).
- D3D12 default on Windows (4.6) batching behaviour for floor-mark draws (spike S2): HIGH.
- Y-sorted CanvasItem layer ordering and z_index bands (draw-call batching, `I_wall`): LOW.
- Sprite2D / MultiMeshInstance2D with nearest texture filter, integer positioning: LOW.
- Light2D / shadow-mask sets interacting with batch splits (`L_sets`, written by Lighting, not this system): LOW to MEDIUM.
- Tween/Timer explicitly unused; `RefCounted` resolver, static typing: LOW.
